#1966. Max Dowman breaks Jude Bellingham record: what makes the Arsenal gem so special?

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 11:31

Max Dowman, who turns 17 soon, has already made history in the Premier League, the Champions League and for England

It seems that every piece of news about Max Dowman starts the same way: the young Arsenal player has broken another record. At 16, the Englishman has already been the youngest player to score in the Premier League, to play in the Champions League and to win the English league title.

This week, he added two more marks to the list: he became the youngest player to represent the England Under-21s and, three days later, the youngest to score for the side, surpassing records that belonged to Jude Bellingham.

The question is not only how many more records he can break, but what makes Dowman such a special talent and how far his characteristics can take him. The combination of individual skill, ball carrying, strength to compete physically and understanding of the game helps to explain why he can already produce against much older opponents.

Dowman was born on 31 December 2009 and joined Arsenal as a child. His progress through the youth ranks was so rapid that, at 13, he was already playing for the Under-18s. In September 2024, aged 14 years and eight months, he made his debut in the UEFA Youth League, an Under-19 competition, and became the youngest scorer in the history of the tournament.

The midfielder began training with the first team at 14 and took part in the 2025 pre-season. In August of that year, aged 15 years and 235 days, he made his Premier League debut against Leeds United. He was the second-youngest player to appear in the competition’s history, behind only Ethan Nwaneri, his Arsenal team-mate.

In November 2025, an even more significant milestone arrived. Coming on in the 3-0 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the tournament’s history, aged 15 years and 308 days. He was also the first 15-year-old to play in the competition.

The 2025-26 season brought two more high-profile records. In March, he scored against Everton and, aged 16 years and 73 days, became the youngest scorer in Premier League history, beating James Vaughan’s mark by 197 days.

Months later, he went down in Arsenal history as the youngest player to win the Premier League. The medal came at 16 years and 144 days, when the club ended a 22-year wait for the title. In October, he received three Guinness World Records certificates for the achievements.

Now, the England Under-21s have added two more chapters. Dowman made his debut for the side against Portugal on 13 November, aged 16 years and 317 days, surpassing Bellingham’s mark as the youngest player to represent the age group. On the following Monday, he started for the first time and scored the winning goal against France, aged 16 years and 320 days. Bellingham had scored his first Under-21 goal aged 17 years and 67 days.

Records broken for Arsenal and England (born 31/12/2009)

If he scores for the senior England team before 12/11/2027, Dowman will surpass Wayne Rooney (17 years and 317 days, in 2003) as the youngest scorer for England.

Age in years (y) and days (d) on the date of each record. n/a = previous holder not confirmed by an official source. Data up to 17/11/2026.

Sources: Arsenal, Premier League, ESPN and TNT Sports

Dowman’s main characteristic is his ability to carry the ball and beat opponents. He finds it easy to receive under pressure, shield possession with his body and change direction in tight spaces. He does not rely on straight-line speed alone: he uses feints, changes of pace and short movements to unbalance defenders.

Dowman already had a physique that allowed him to compete with older players, but he has also developed an intelligent way of using his body to protect the ball. That explains why he does not seem so intimidated when facing professional defenders.

Left-footed, he usually plays on the right, from where he can cut inside and use his dominant foot. The position also allows him to receive wide, draw the opposing full-back and choose between accelerating towards the box, combining with a team-mate or finding a pass inside. His ball control and ability to change the direction of play make him a particularly difficult threat to handle one-on-one.

But reducing him to a dribbling winger would ignore an important part of his repertoire. Dowman also has experience playing as an attacking midfielder and in deeper roles. In the youth ranks, he even played as a deep-lying midfielder. This variety helped him develop a broader understanding of space and the different roles on the pitch.

That versatility is an advantage for Arteta. At Arsenal, Dowman has already been used on the right and in central positions. When he receives between the lines, he can turn quickly and carry the ball towards the opposition defence. If he starts wide, he can attack the space between full-back and centre-back, moving closer to the box to shoot or take part in a combination.

There are also signs that his play without the ball matches his technical quality. In the win over France, Lee Carsley highlighted the teenager’s defensive performance, as he dropped back to intercept a pass and joined the pressing of opponents. A willingness to recover, press and take part in collective actions is an important requirement for earning a place in a side like Arteta’s.

Dowman’s rise inevitably prompts comparisons. His path recalls, in some respects, that of Nwaneri, who also made his Arsenal debut very young and had to find space in a competitive squad. Both came through the youth ranks playing in central positions, but had their first opportunities in the first team on the right.

The difference is that Dowman seems to have an even clearer ability to carry the ball at speed and beat opponents one-on-one. That does not mean it is possible to determine who will have the more successful career.

Arsenal also have reason to manage expectations. The recent episode against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup highlighted one area of concern. After suffering a heavy challenge, the teenager reacted and was sent off, receiving a three-match ban. Arteta criticised the player publicly and said professional football is not an environment protected from provocation and the consequences of one’s own actions.

There is also the question of workload. A player who starts playing professional matches so early needs physical and emotional support. Arsenal have recent experience of integrating young players such as Saka, Nwaneri and Lewis-Skelly, but each athlete has his own process.

His first professional contract will be signed when he turns 17 on 31 December, after he agreed a pre-contract with Arsenal in January. The decision to stay at the club is important for the continuity of a development that has been closely monitored since the youth ranks.

The path to the senior England team is also open, but does not need to be taken immediately. Bellingham, who lost the Under-21 records to Dowman, played only four matches at that level before being promoted to the senior team.

For now, the best way to assess Dowman is to look at what he can already do, without turning every record into a career prediction. The rest depends on development, opportunities and careful management.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

‘He’s one of our own and he’s still an important player. It’s true that he’s not playing right now, although he’s ready if the manager needs him.’

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

The Red Devils ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options, though, which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a new long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked in recent months.

#1958. Barnsley FC's Cieran Slicker and Daniel Stendel call for fans to unite against Sheffield Wednesday

Fans group Tykes Union are encouraging supporters to gather outside the ground before kick-off to protest against the running of the club, with a chant planned four minutes into the game to mark the number of years the current regime has been in charge.

But with 5,700 away fans expected to make up a third of the crowd and much more concentrated in the away end, Slicker says their Barnsley counterparts have an important part to play, just as they did when the young team battled to win a point against Oxford United despite a ninth-minute red card for Jack Shepherd.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"I go back to the example of the Oxford game when we conceded and you feel the lift almost from the crowd and it was refreshing," says the goalkeeper. "It did give us that almost second wind.

"Whether it's the home crowd, the away crowd, I think there's a buzz from both. There might be a few beer bottles up at my head or whatever but I thrive off that (atmosphere) and I'm excited for being at both ends of the pitch.

"The crowd is there, you feel it but in reality, it doesn't change my focus.

"You could have no people watching, you could be training, but still as focused as what I will be whenever really.

"You might hear more and even the communication might be different but I think it's still focused, even more focused maybe.

"Communication as a goalkeeper is one of the most important aspects. I'm going to try and communicate whether the boys hear it or not.

"They might be quite glad that they're not hearing my voice."

Stendel is without the suspended Cameron McGeehan and Luca Connell is a doubt with illness, so he hopes the fans can compensate.

"What I would like is that we have a big support in the game," he says. "Not just because it's a derby but also these young guys, without the captain (McGeehan), need the push from the stands.

"It was really positive in the last big game against Oxford here. With ten men after nine minutes, they pushed the team so much."

This is Slicker's first South Yorkshire derby, and he is fully aware of its importance.

"When I first joined, looking at the stadium, I walked around sort of imagining it full,” he recalls.

"There's a lot of (Yorkshire) derbies in League One but Sheffield Wednesday will be the big one – one of, if not the biggest, game of my career.

"I played for Scotland internationally. This will probably be a similar level to it."

If a win would do wonders for Barnsley's belief after nine games without a league victory, wins at Oakwell are special for away teams who bring a big following.

"In terms of an away stand, for a big club, it's a brilliant one," comments Sheffield Wednesday manager Dave Challinor. "That end will be full, it won't be half in one bit, half in the other.

"It's a huge stand. We've got to make the biggest advantage of that we can."

#1957. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

#1953. Wes Brown: ‘Man Utd still have every chance of Champions League qualification’

Wes Brown believes Manchester United should still be aiming for a top-five finish this season after Mauricio Pochettino was appointed head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has officially taken the reins at Old Trafford after his final two matches with the United States national team.

Pochettino has undoubtedly been thrown in at the deep end, with United winless in their last eight Premier League matches and facing Liverpool in his first game on Sunday.

But former Red Devils defender Brown believes that the Argentine has the quality to inspire a quick turnaround from his new crop of players.

‘Poch is very experienced, and he has his own style of play, but it’s all about consistency, he told Metro. ‘Making the players believe they’re good enough and making sure they do it week in, week out.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We’ve had no momentum; we’ve played well here and there in games, and when we did we managed to score, but at the same time we’ve been very poor at times and open to teams scoring at will, making loads of mistakes.

‘The confidence isn’t there, but he’ll be coming in and just trying to get consistency through the team.

‘When a new manager comes in, the players really make an effort, that’s just the way it goes, but then it’s up to the manager to keep that going through the season, and whether or not he’ll be able to, we’ll all have to see.’

Pochettino brings with him extensive experience in the Premier League but also a proven track record of nurturing young talent into the first team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

And Brown is hopeful that academy duo Shea Lacey and Harry Amass could benefit from the Argentine’s arrival, adding: ‘If anyone, you think those two might come in and get a game under the new manager to show what they can do.

‘I think at the moment, you are looking at Shea Lacey and thinking, “Yeah, he can get a game”. He delivers, he runs, he works hard.

Pochettino faces a trip to Anfield for his first game in charge (Picture: Getty)

‘But I also think when you’re in a position where you don’t necessarily just bring in the young lads as well. I think that’s a tough gig if I’m being honest, and you can’t just bring them in when the team’s like this.’

Pochettino will have to endure a frenetic start to life in the United dugout, with a run of eight games in 21 days starting at Anfield on Sunday.

But with plenty of the season still ahead, Brown thinks United should still be aiming high if they can start fast under their seventh permanent boss since Alex Ferguson’s retirement.

‘There’s still a chance of getting into Europe, 100 per cent,’ Brown added.

‘Even though it’s been very disappointing, even if you look at the table now, the gap is not that big. It’s maybe 8-9 points from a European place, if that.

‘So you’ve still got to have that in the back of your mind. It’s Manchester United; that’s where you aim to be, if not higher, and I’m sure Poch will definitely be looking to get us in that sort of area and going in that direction.’

#1952. When are the 2026-27 Nations League quarter-finals? Dates, fixtures, teams, how they qualified

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 11:57

The 2026-27 UEFA Nations League quarter-finals will take place in March 2027.

The draw for the final eight will take place on November 20, 2026, where it will be decided which teams will face off against each other for a spot in the semi-finals.

Here, Sports Mole runs through all of the details surrounding next year's matches, including dates, fixtures and how each of the eight teams booked a spot in the quarter-finals.

The first legs of the respective last-eight contests will take place between March 25 and March 27, 2027, with the second legs occurring between March 28 and March 30, 2027.

The draw for the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 Nations League will take place at 11am UK time on November 20 at UEFA's headquarters.

Finishing first in the section means that home advantage is gained for the second leg, while the winners of each group will take on a runner-up from another section.

France, Germany, England and Portugal have been the group winners, with Belgium, Netherlands, Spain and Norway qualifying as runners-up in each section.

Portugal are the holders of the Nations League trophy and also the most successful side in the history of the competition, having won it twice (2019 and 2025).

Spain (2023) and France (2021) have also won the tournament.

Germany, England, Belgium, Netherlands and Norway could become first-time winners of the Nations League in 2026-27, with the final set to take place in June 2027.

France finished first in Group A1 to secure a spot in the quarter-finals of the tournament, claiming 13 points from their six matches, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat.

Belgium were second in Group A2, one point behind the section winners France, having claimed 12 points from their six games, boasting a record of four wins and two defeats from six games.

Germany finished at the top of Group A2 with 11 points from six matches. Incredibly, each of Germany, Netherlands and Greece had 11 points from six games, but Germany finished at the summit on UEFA''s head-to-head goal difference tiebreaker.

Netherlands managed to sneak second spot in Group A2 ahead of Greece on overall goal difference, with Xavi's team finishing with a record of three wins, two draws and one defeat from six matches.

England spectacularly secured first position in Group A3 courtesy of their standout 3-2 success over Spain in Madrid on Sunday night; the Three Lions won five and lost one of their six games to collect 15 points, and they ultimately had a better overall goal difference.

Spain were bumped back down to second spot in Group A3 due to their loss to England; the reverse to the Three Lions proved to be their first defeat in 90 minutes since March 2024.

Portugal finished at the top of Group A4, boasting 15 points from their six matches, in order to comfortably secure a position in the quarter-finals of the tournament.

Norway managed to sneak into second spot in Group A4 ahead of Denmark on the final matchday, recording a 3-2 success over the Danes, which gave them the advance in the head-to-head tiebreaker.

#1950. Andriy Shevchenko demands apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk over ‘baseless’ failed drugs test claims

Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.

Speaking to YouTube channel Guest of Gordon this week, Mudryk was asked who he felt was to blame for the adverse finding.

‘The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,’ Mudryk said.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘It should never have existed. I probably haven’t said it publicly yet but I’m saying it now.

‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.’

Asked how meldonium got into his system, Mudryuk said: ‘The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

‘There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Chelsea striker Shevchenko, who is now the president of the Ukrainian Association of Football, has hit back at Mudryk’s claims and has described the winger’s version of events as ‘baseless slander’.

‘I want to express my position on the accusations of Mykhailo Mudryk. Loud statements were made about the UAF, the Ukrainian national team. This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,’ Shevchenko said in a statement to Tribuna Ukraine.

‘Instead, after the suspension of Mykhailo Mudryk, his representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to artificially find an employee who would take responsibility for the appearance of meldonium in his doping sample.

‘The UAF refused – such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work. The accusations from Mykhailo’s representatives were not confirmed or proven after many studies and inspections. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English association confirm this.

‘After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during the national team training camp. The team staff complied with this request.

‘Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also agreed for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him during the training camp. These people monitored his regimen and recovery and helped him with his daily life.

‘The UAF has completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and have been in contact with those who worked on the case.

‘I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism

‘If Mykhailo has evidence to support his words, let him provide it. If there is no such evidence, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he questioned.’

#1949. Arsenal injury update: Martin Zubimendi, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka latest return dates

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal do not have many fitness concerns ahead of their return to Premier League action, but Martin Zubimendi is a big doubt to face Newcastle this weekend.

The Gunners head to St James’ Park looking to build on victories over Liverpool and Hull prior to the international break, with manager Mikel Arteta expected to have a near fully fit senior squad to choose from.

Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman are guaranteed to miss out through injury and suspension respectively, while Zubimendi’s involvement is up in the air after he limped off during Spain’s 3-2 loss to England in the Nations League.

That same game saw Ezri Konsa shake off a knock to start - and score - thus proving his fitness as he bid to keep his place in the Arsenal defence now that William Saliba has recovered from a back injury.

There was also a mini scare involving Christos Tzolis as he was sent for an MRI while on international duty with Greece, but any fears were immediately allayed and the winger played 88 minutes of the 1-0 win over Serbia.

With that in mind, here is the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates…

The Spaniard just is not having much luck this season. Having gone from the first choice midfield partner for Declan Rice to fourth choice, Zubimendi was already finding opportunities limited prior to this latest knock.

Keep in mind that Zubimendi has been playing with a protective face mask in recent weeks due to suffering a broken nose against Everton nearly a month ago, he suffered a further blow when forced off in the second half for Spain against England.

After the match, Luis de la Fuente confirmed the Arsenal star had sustained a muscle injury, though its severity remains unknown as he will have returned to London Colney for further tests.

A further update should be provided by Arteta in the pre-Newcastle press conference, but it would be a surprise if Zubimendi is able to play again before the end of the month.

Saliba should be challenging Konsa and Gabriel for a place in the Arsenal defence this weekend, following a delayed start to the season due to a long-term back injury that he exacerbated while on duty for France at the World Cup.

An unused substitute in the Champions League victory over Slavia Prague, Saliba and was then left out completely against Hull, before getting some minutes under his belt for the U21s as he played one half of a 5-2 win over Aston Villa.

It has since been reported that the Frenchman played in another behind-closed-doors friendly during the week after not being selected by Zinedine Zidane for the Nations League double-header.

With Arsenal entering a hectic period in terms of fixtures, it should not be too long before Saliba is back in first team action.

Though, the form of Konsa and Gabriel does mean Arteta can ease the defender in.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Newcastle (A)

Saka has now missed five Arsenal games in a row with a quad injury sustained after just 10 minutes against Bayern Munich last month.

He was also be sidelined for England’s Nations League double-header against Croatia and Spain during the international break.

Amid fears Saka could be out for action for up to eight weeks, Arteta confirmed that the winger’s recovery was going well ahead of the Hull fixture, but it will still be some weeks until he can make a full comeback.

”The way it happened, it wasn't a really aggressive action,” Arteta said before the 1-0 win over Hull.

“So that gives you some hope as well that the tissue will repair in a more efficient and faster way as well and he has some very good symptoms right now. So we have to wait and see."

#1948. Manchester United shortlist £26m Spurs target to solve Mauricio Pochettino issue

Manchester United are considering a move for Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at United this week having replaced Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the international break.

But the Argentine begins his tenure at Old Trafford without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United have made funds available to strengthen Pochettino’s squad in January and the club are targeting a new striker.

According to The i Paper, Matanovic is on United’s striker shortlist alongside Folarin Balogun, who Monaco are open to selling in the January transfer window.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The report adds that United are also looking to bolster Pochettino’s defence with Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey and left-back Antonee Robinson under consideration.

Matanovic, meanwhile, was signed by Freiburg in an €8 million (£6.8m) deal from Eintracht Frankfurt last year.

The Croatia international, who offers a physical presence in attack at 6ft 5in, has scored 23 goals in 64 games for Freiburg so far.

At international level, Matanovic has scored two goals in 17 appearances for Croatia and came off the bench in three games at the World Cup in the summer.

Matanovic, who is now valued at around €30m (£26m), has also been linked with a move to Tottenham.

When asked about his future in September, Matanovic insisted he had not received an approach to leave Freiburg.

#1947. Chelsea injury update: Joao Pedro, Emi Martinez, Reece James latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea could well have two key men back when they welcome Leeds this weekend.

The Blues were beaten 1-0 by Sunderland just before the international break, and they have been without a number of stars, which has left Xabi Alonso with a headache.

The west Londoners have dropped to fifth in the Premier League table as a result of the defeat, but they are hoping to have some of their big names back on Saturday.

With that in mind, here is the latest Chelsea injury news and return dates…

Acheampong was left out of the squad at the Stadium of Light, which was a surprise having started all five games before that.

Alonso revealed, however, that the youngster was dealing with a minor knock, and he withdrew from international duty with England’s under-21 side.

“He is recovering from a minor thing,” Alonso said after Sunderland.

“He missed the fitness to be ready for today but we are expecting that he will be back after the international break,” Alonso said of Acheampong before the defeat to Sunderland. “It’s a pity because he was in a good moment.

“There are situations. Yesterday Josh felt something and he was not fit to play. So we are shorter in options and we need to go through this time.

“Even when we win, or when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting to have them back because they are important.

“Now we need to use the time to recover them, but with the players we have, we have to get ready for the next one.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

No1 Martinez has been out for four matches after he broke his jaw.

He was clattered by Jarrad Branthwaite against Everton, and was forced to have surgery.

The Argentine was scheduled to be sidelined for six weeks, but he has already returned to training, albeit not being risked against Sunderland.

"He has made a great effort to be available but probably it was too rash, too risky [to be selected],” Alonso said.

“So he will use one more week, 10 days, to keep on training and get used to the mask. I’m sure after the break he will be available.”

#1946. Athletic Bilbao vs Espanyol - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 11:58, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:33

Athletic Bilbao will be bidding to continue their strong run of form when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Espanyol on Friday night.

The Lions have won three and drawn one of their last four matches in all competitions, while Espanyol have managed to pick up four points from their last two La Liga fixtures.

Athletic have a record of four wins, four draws and three defeats from their 11 league matches this season, with 16 points leaving them in seventh spot in the La Liga table.

The Basque outfit entered the international break off the back of a 1-1 draw with Osasuna, but they have managed to pick up seven points from their last three fixtures.

Edin Terzic's side also managed to progress in the Copa del Rey with a 6-1 win over Prat at the end of October, so it has been a successful period in their season, losing only one of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

Athletic have won 88, drawn 42 and lost 71 of their previous 201 matches in all competitions with Espanyol, but they have actually lost the last two games between the two teams, including a 2-0 reverse in their last league fixture on May 2026.

The Lions are winless in their last three fixtures with Espanyol, but they did win three straight fixtures against the Catalan team between January 2023 and October 2024.

Espanyol entered the international break off the back of a goalless draw with Deportivo La Coruna, while their last away fixture brought a 1-0 victory over Villarreal.

The Catalan team boast a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches, with 12 points leaving them in 13th spot in the division.

Eder Sarabia took charge of Espanyol at the end of October, and the immediate improvement has been obvious, claiming four points from his two league games at the helm.

Espanyol were excellent in the first half of last season and had the look of a team potentially capable of finishing in the Champions League spot, but a disappointing second half of the campaign saw them ultimately finish 11th.

The White and Blues have picked up seven points from their six away league matches this season, and they recorded a 2-1 victory over Athletic in the corresponding fixture at San Mames during the 2025-26 campaign.

Athletic will again be missing Maroan Sannadi, Gorka Guruzeta and Unai Eguiluz through injury, while Aitor Paredes and Nico Serrano are doubts at this stage of proceedings.

Unai Simon, Aymeric Laporte and Nico Williams all featured for Spain over the international break, and the trio are set to be in the starting side on Friday night.

There could also be a return to the starting side for Oihan Sancet, while Inaki Williams is likely to keep his spot through the middle for the Basque outfit.

As for Espanyol, Roger Hinojo is available again after serving a suspension against Deportivo before the international break, but Kike Garcia, Jofre Carreras and Urko Gonzalez are expected to miss out due to injury problems.

Alex Calatrava has ruptured the cruciate ligament in his left knee, meanwhile, and the attacker is facing a lengthy period out.

Roberto Fernandez has scored six times in 12 appearances for the White and Blues this season, and the 24-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be a return to the side for Bryan Zaragoza, who dropped down to the bench for the clash with Deportivo.

Athletic Bilbao possible starting lineup:

Simon; Rincon, Vivian, Laporte, Berchiche; Canales, Gerenabarrena; Berenguer, Sancet, N Williams; I Williams

Fortuno; El Hilali, Cabrera, Hartman; Dolan, Exposito, Lozano, Hinojo; Milla; Zaragoza, Fernandez

Espanyol are capable of making this a tricky match for Athletic, but we are expecting the Basque outfit to gather a valuable three points on Friday evening.

Tottenham are back in action in the Premier League when they take on Ipswich on Saturday.

Spurs lost to Leeds last time out to snap their three-game winning streak, and they lost a key man in the defeat at Elland Road.

There are also question marks of a number of players ahead of their return to league football this weekend.

Here is all the latest Tottenham injury news and return dates.

The Frenchman is set to be sidelined for a significant period after suffering a “bad injury” at Leeds, which left him on crutches after the game.

The winger was challenged hard, studs-up, by Jayden Bogle, and he was forced off in the second half before being seen in a medical boot post-match.

He missed out international duty with the France U21s, with the French Football Federation stating: “Having suffered an injury with his club Tottenham, Mathys Tel is forced to withdraw from the France Under-21 team training camp which began on Monday at the CNF Clairefontaine.”

It still remains to be seen how long Tel will be sidelined for, with a further update likely to follow when De Zerbi speaks to the media ahead of Ipswich.

He has not featured since picking up a knock against Chelsea last month, and De Zerbi said of the attacking midfielder after the Leeds loss: “James, I thought [about bringing him on] in the last substitution before Luca Williams-Barnett, but I saw [Mohammed] Kudus was very tired.

“And James didn’t [train] until Thursday. On Thursday he worked half [and] part of the training yesterday.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

He is thought to be back and ready to play against Ipswich this weekend.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Ipswich (H)

Tosin has been out with a calf injury since making his first start of the season last month, in a win over Coventry, but was back in training heading into the international break.

#1944. Lampard: Decisions went against Coventry in defeat to Everton

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Frank Lampard was still left questioning the decisions made during Coventry City's 3-1 defeat to Everton as they prepare to bounce back against Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Coventry signed off for the international break with a loss at Hill Dickinson Stadium, despite taking the lead through Yann Gboho's 52nd-minute strike past Jordan Pickford.

However, Thierno Barry led Everton's fightback with two goals before teeing up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, though Lampard expressed his confusion about some of the decisions.

And on Wednesday, the independent Key Match Incidents panel concluded that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski fouled Caleb Yirenkyi.

There was also wide-scale debate over Thierno Barry's second goal and whether it was handball, with the Everton forward squeezing the ball in at Carl Rushworth's near post.

"It's a game we lost because of decisions, in my opinion," Lampard told reporters of those findings. "There were decisions that went wrongly against us by the referee.

"I appreciate they were honest after the event, but that doesn't help us. Going away from home is not easy, but I felt like we deserved a result. We must keep going.

"These things happen in football so we have to keep positive and keep going."

Thank you for your support on the road this evening, safe travels home. https://t.co/FFMkr8xTAh

— Coventry City (@CoventryCityFC) November 6, 2026

There will be a new face in the Palace dugout at the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend, with Thomas Frank set to take charge of his first game with the Eagles.

Frank was appointed as Palace's new boss following the sacking of Pierre Sage, who left the club sitting bottom of the Premier League after 10 matches.

Only two of Palace's 13 previous permanent managers in the Premier League have won their first game in charge (D4 L7 – first spells only), with Alan Pardew beating Tottenham in January 2015 and Oliver Glasner beating Burnley in February 2024.

And when asked about his hopes for the rest of the season, Frank outlined his ambition to help Palace compete on all fronts, including the EFL Cup and Europa League.

"Of course, I've looked at the team and done a lot of analysis on the team. I think there's a lot of positives, definitely," Frank said.

"There's no doubt, to state the obvious, that we need to stabilise things. That's one thing. We need to work incredibly hard.

"Obviously, we're conceding too many goals that we need to address, so we need to work on the defensive side of things with principles, attitude, everything regarding that.

"Then, of course, it's one game at a time. We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe. There are two fantastic cup tournaments, but, of course, the Premier League is the most important, if we need to prioritise. But we would like to compete on all fronts."

Rudoni is one of six players who are both their team's leading shot taker (17) and chance creator (17) in the top-flight this season, alongside Chelsea's Cole Palmer, Palace's Yeremy Pino, Ipswich Town's Julio Enciso, Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes, and Newcastle United's Harvey Barnes.

He is also the only Coventry City player to score more than once in the Premier League this season (three).

Despite falling to a 3-1 defeat against Liverpool ahead of the international break, one positive for Palace was to see Nketiah get himself on the scoresheet.

Nketiah scored his first goal in the Premier League this season, netting for the first time since December 2025 against Fulham, and with Jean-Philippe Mateta still serving a suspension, Frank could give him the nod up front ahead of Jorgen Strand Larsen.

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 16, 2026

This is the first meeting between Coventry and Crystal in any competition since March 2012, a 1-1 draw in the Championship.

Coventry have lost just one of their six Premier League games against Palace (W2 D3), with this the first meeting since a 3-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 1998.

The Sky Blues have, however, lost seven or more of their opening 10 games of a league campaign for only the third time ever, also doing so in their first two Football League seasons in 1919-20 (nine) and 1920-21 (seven). It is already as many defeats as they suffered in last season's Championship.

But they face a Palace side that have conceded 24 goals in 10 Premier League games this season, their most at this stage of a season since 1980-81 under Terry Venables (also 24).

Indeed, 10 of the 15 sides to have conceded that many goals in their first 10 Premier League games have been relegated, though Wolves did it most recently in 2024-25 (27 conceded) and ended the season in 16th.

Palace won their first four visits to the Coventry Building Society Arena between 2005 and 2008 but are winless in their last four in all competitions between 2009 and 2012 (D2 L2), making Frank's debut all the more tricky.

#1943. Liverpool injury update: Virgil van Dijk, Giovanni Leoni, Jeremie Frimpong latest news and return dates

Liverpool have been handed a double defensive boost ahead of the Premier League clash with Manchester United.

It has been a mixed international break for Andoni Iraola’s side on the injury front, with concerns over Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai.

However, there was some positive news, as star striker Alexander Isak was rested by Sweden on Tuesday night, meaning he should be fully fresh and raring to go on Sunday afternoon.

With that in mind, here is the latest Liverpool injury news and return dates…

Leoni is one of two Liverpool players reported by The Athletic to have returned to first team training after a long injury lay-off.

The Italian has missed a full year of action since suffering an ACL injury, with further issues in his knee. Originally pencilled for a September return, the complications have pushed Leoni’s comeback to December.

Head coach Iraola explained: “It’s taking more time than we wanted. The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.”

However, despite a return to training, it is expected that Leoni is still a few weeks away from being in contention for some playing time.

Potential return date: Saturday December 12, vs Leeds (H)

Conor Bradley is the other long-term absentee back in first-team training. The Northern Ireland international suffered bone and ligament damage in his knee against Arsenal in January.

Bradley was predicted to resume training with the first team during the international break, implying that he is keeping pace with his expected recovery.

#1942. Nascar, Nets, Big 12 and MSE: Yormark’s appointment and how he can help Milan

AC Milan were introduced to a new name this week: Brett Yormark. But who is he and what does he bring to the table?

With Milan’s announcement of a new company – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE company.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

In terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

After his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime shows.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment company, he leaves behind a role with Big 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

Given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the company take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.
