#1940. Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius to Arsenal; Nusa bid; Man Utd plot Paz talks; Chelsea, Liverpool latest

The January transfer window is fast approaching, with Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham all looking to strengthen their squads ahead of the second half of the season. Arsenal are among the clubs interested in Como midfielder Nico Paz, although they face competition from Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain. Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa are also on the Gunners’ radar, while Vinicius Junior has reportedly emerged as a target once again.

Mauricio Pochettino officially begins his tenure as Manchester United manager today and could make Calvin Bassey his first signing. The former Chelsea boss is keen to shore up a defence that has struggled this season, with the Fulham defender potentially offering a solution. Pochettino is also set to face the media ahead of United’s meeting with Liverpool as preparations continue.

Chelsea are confident of securing a deal for Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott when the window opens, despite the Cherries insisting he is not for sale. Liverpool are also monitoring Mexican youngster Gilberto Mora, while the Reds are now leading the race for Lamine Camara, who came close to joining Chelsea on deadline day in the summer. Follow all the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Fulham are in talks with captain Calvin Bassey over a new contract as they look to fend off interest from Manchester United, writes Standard Sport’s Sam Tabuteau.

The 26-year-old centre-back, whose contract expires next summer, is understood to be on United’s shortlist as they look to sign defensive reinforcements in January.

Fulham hold the option to extend Bassey’s current deal by a further year.

The Cottagers are keen to keep hold of Bassey, especially after Alvaro Arbeloa promoted him to captain in the summer.

Nothing has been agreed yet, but Fulham have opened talks with Bassey over a new contract and do not intend to sell him in January.

Thomas Frank has confirmed Crystal Palace are working to appoint Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, with a deal “very close.”

Frank was appointed the Eagles’ head coach this week, replacing the Frenchman Pierre Sage, who lasted just 16 matches in the job and left the club dead last in the Premier League.

As he looks to establish his coaching staff, though, Frank is looking into a reunion with Cueva. The pair were colleagues at Brentford between 2020 and 2024, when Cueva was poached by the Blues, who reportedly spent £1m to secure his services.

But Chelsea have upgraded on Cueva this season, signing Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee in a similarly pricey move.

Palace have reportedly been in talks with Chelsea over Cueva’s transfer for some time, and Frank, speaking in his first press conference since taking over, has now confirmed the widespread reports that a deal is imminent.

Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is attracting a growing number of suiters, including Arsenal.

Fichajes reports that an impressive run of form in Belgium has alerted a number of Premier League clubs.

The 22-year-old has revitalised his career after difficult spells at Ajax and Wolves, producing five goals and eight assists in 15 appearances across all competitions this season.

Arsenal are continuing their search for a marquee forward ahead of the January transfer window.

Sky Sports report that the Premier League champions are tracking RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa and Brentford’s Kevin Schade as potential options, with a preference for a left-sided attacker capable of playing across the frontline.

Arsenal are also monitoring Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and could sell a midfielder to compete with Chelsea and Liverpool for the 23-year-old’s signature.

Manchester United have joined Tottenham in the race to sign Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis as Mauricio Pochettino looks to strengthen his attack in January.

The 27-year-old has scored 19 goals in 19 appearances across all competitions this season, attracting interest from several clubs.

CaughtOffside report that Pavlidis is open to a Premier League move, while United are also monitoring Victor Osimhen, Ivan Toney and Serhou Guirassy.

Pochettino is expected to receive backing in January as he looks to improve his squad, with defensive reinforcements also being considered.

Nico Paz is a transfer target for Manchester United following Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment as manager.

The Sun reports that Paz, who has sent a timely reminder of his talent after scoring two stunning goals for Argentina in their 7-0 victory over Costa Rica, is on United’s radar ahead of the January window.

Real Madrid retain an €80m option to re-sign Paz in 2027, while Arsenal, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain are also believed to be monitoring the Argentine.

Born in Tenerife, he began his career at Real Madrid before moving to Como in 2024.

Chelsea’s former techincal director Michael Emenalo has taken up an advisory role at Leicester City.

The Athletic reports that the Nigerian, who was with the Blues for five and a half years, is part of a team of consultants that is helping the Foxes with their future planning.

Manchester United are set to back Mauricio Pochettino the January transfer window.

Sky Sports reports that the Red Devils are prepared to sanction some signings for their new manager in the winter, with the club currently sat in the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino, who arrived at Carrington to begin work on Wednesday, will be tasked with guiding United away from the bottom three and as high up the top-flight table as he can, while also seeing how far he can get his new side in the Champions League.

Mauricio Pochettino has listed the three things he is hoping to bring to Manchester United in his first message to fans.

The Argentine arrived at his new club on Wednesday, touching down in Manchester immediately after overseeing his final game in charge of the United States.

In his first message to United fans, posted to the club’s social media channels, he said: “I am looking forward to meeting you guys.

“I have heard so many good things about you. I hope we bring all the happiness, working together and connect[ion], so that it is going to be a special season, and to make our players fight on the field and get the results we deserve.”

Manchester United have confirmed the departures of five members of staff after Mauricio Pochettino began work as the club’s new manager on Wednesday.

The Argentine was pictured arriving at Carrington for his first day in charge of the Red Devils, having flown immediately over after his final match with the United States.

#1939. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#1938. Mauricio Pochettino has already introduced a Tottenham tradition at Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino is having to squeeze a lot into his first days as Manchester United, but there will be time for one tried-and-tested tradition.

The Argentine touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, just hours after overseeing USA’s 2-0 win over Haiti in Cincinnati. The new head coach has conducted his first interview with club media, posed for photos and met the players.

On Thursday, Pochettino will take charge of his first training session at the club’s Carrington base before conducting his first press conference on Friday ahead of his first game on Sunday, which is a daunting trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool.

But there will see be time for a team dinner.

The Independent report that Pochettino plans on taking the players and staff out for a team bonding evening, and he will be picking up the tab.

It is a tradition Pochettino is said to have first introduced the custom during his time at Southampton, believing it was an important way to build relationships and strengthen the bond within a squad. He then did it at Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

It has previously been reported elsewhere that Pochettino held team dinners a number of times during his five-and-a-half-year tenure at Spurs.

With Pochettino taking charge midway through the campaign, there is no opportunity for a traditional pre-season or an extended period to get to know his players. The dinner will therefore provide an early chance for the 54-year-old and his coaching staff to assess the group's dynamics away from the training pitch.

Pochettino believes creating a strong sense of togetherness is essential to success, and the gathering will allow him to begin establishing his approach at Old Trafford. It will also give players and staff an opportunity to get to know their new manager and his backroom team in a more relaxed setting.

With a demanding schedule ahead, Pochettino will hope the occasion helps lay the foundations for a successful union between players and staff.

#1937. Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils to consider legal action over JJ Gabriel's Real Madrid move?

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 12:44

Manchester United are reportedly prepared to take legal action over JJ Gabriel's proposed move to Real Madrid if they uncover any evidence of inducement.

Gabriel revealed back in September that he wanted to leave Old Trafford after failing to break into the senior team.

Although he remains registered with the club until the end of the season, that would not prevent him from moving elsewhere in the European Union once he turns 16.

A host of clubs were interested in signing the youngster, but it now appears that he is set to join Real Madrid.

Gabriel posted a farewell message to Man Utd supporters, thanking the club for their role in his development, but the Red Devils are understood to be angered by his decision.

According to the Manchester Evening News, the Red Devils were disappointed that the video was posted without any prior contact from Gabriel's representatives.

Man Utd have reportedly made several attempts to check on the teenager's welfare since he requested to leave, but have been unable to establish contact with his family.

Meanwhile, agency Epic Sports has become Gabriel's new representative, with the club believing that the youngster has been poorly advised by his father throughout the process.

The Red Devils are prepared to explore every available legal avenue should evidence of inducement from Madrid emerge, given the strict regulations surrounding the recruitment of players under the age of 18.

The youngster only turned 16 on October 6, and there was little reason to believe that his pathway to the first team would have been blocked at Old Trafford.

Critics may argue that Man Utd could have handled his development better, perhaps following Barcelona's approach with Lamine Yamal, although such success stories are relatively rare.

What appears particularly surprising is Gabriel's decision to join Real Madrid, where he would face competition from the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Arda Guler, Endrick and Yan Diomande for a place in the senior side.

Man Utd can hardly be held solely responsible for his decision, but the way this saga has unfolded could raise questions about the club's ability to retain and nurture its most promising young talents.

#1936. Premier League predictions: Pochettino starts life at Man Utd against rivals Liverpool

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of the latest weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season following the latest international break.

During the two-week hiatus, there were two managerial changes, with Mauricio Pochettino replacing Michael Carrick at Manchester United, who sit in the relegation zone, and Thomas Frank succeeding Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace, who prop up the table.

At the other end of the standings, Arsenal hold a five-point lead, having won each of their last five matches.

They sit above high-flying Brighton, while Manchester City slipped down to third following three straight losses.

Matchday 11 sees fixtures take place on Saturday, Sunday and Monday, and ahead of what should be another enticing group of Premier League fixtures, we check out the Opta supercomputer's match predictions.

Manchester City's strong start to the season came crashing down before the break, and they are looking to get back to winning ways when they host Fulham on Saturday.

City have lost three straight league games, as many as in their previous 36 (W25 D8); since the start of 2007-08, they have only lost four in a row twice, doing so in August 2008 and December 2024.

However, City have won their last 17 Premier League games against Fulham and have won their last 20 against the Cottagers in all competitions.

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 17, 2026

And our predictive model makes them the favourites to triumph at 66.1%, with no team having a higher win probability across the fixtures this weekend. Fulham's hopes of a win sit at 15.5%.

Fulham struggled at the start of the season, but they are unbeaten in their last four league games (W2 D2) and have lost just one of their last seven (W2 D4).

Onto the 15:00 kick-offs, Aston Villa are looking to bounce back after throwing away a late lead in their thrilling 4-4 draw with Man Utd against Sunderland.

Villa have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight matches against Sunderland (W5 D6), going down 3-1 at the Stadium of Light in January 2016.

And Villa are unbeaten in their last six league games (W3 D3), though they dropped points from winning positions in all three draws.

Sunderland, meanwhile, are looking to win successive Premier League games for the first time this season following their 1-0 victory over Chelsea last time out.

It is Villa who are the favourites to triumph, winning 59.3% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations for Unai Emery's 150th league game in charge, to Sunderland's 19.4%.

A rampant Bournemouth (55.3%) are looking to continue their push up the table against Nottingham Forest (21.6%), who ended their slump against Man City before the break.

The Cherries, who have won each of their last eight matches in all competitions, are unbeaten in all eight of their Premier League games against Forest (W4 D4).

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso will be sweating over the availability of midfield lynchpin Moises Caicedo for Saturday’s Premier League clash with rivals Leeds.

The former Brighton man has featured on international duty with Ecuador, playing 81 minutes and scoring during a 2-0 win over Costa Rica last week.

Caicedo was handed another start in Ecuador’s next friendly with Bolivia earlier this week, only for the midfielder to ask to come off at half-time due to feeling unwell.

After the game Caicedo admitted that he had taken precautions in order to give himself the best chance of being available for Chelsea.

Caicedo explained to reporters: "I didn't feel very well, so I asked to come off instead, because I know I have another commitment with my club.

#1933. Chelsea news: Manager merry-go-round exposes flaws of BlueCo model at Strasbourg

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:46

Has Strasbourg become a prisoner of BlueCo’s strategy? The departure of Hugo Oliveira, replaced by Vitor Matos after only a few months in the dugout, has reignited questions over the management of the Alsatian club.

Only 13th in Ligue 1 with 10 points after 10 games, Strasbourg are going through a very difficult start to the season. But beyond the results, it is above all the absence of continuity that stands out. Since January, four managers have followed one another in the Strasbourg dugout. Such instability is hard to reconcile with building a genuine sporting project.

Liam Rosenior’s departure for Chelsea last January had already given a glimpse of the limits of the model. The Englishman, now at Paris FC, had established a playing identity and allowed Strasbourg to rediscover a certain ambition, before being called up to the flagship club of the BlueCo galaxy.

Gary O’Neil succeeded him, before joining Ipswich Town a few months later. Hugo Oliveira, who arrived this summer, ultimately lasted only four months. Vitor Matos is now expected to succeed him.

This succession of changes raises an obvious question: how do you build a team when its manager changes so regularly?

Each coach arrives with his own principles, tactical preferences and recruitment needs. Rosenior’s high press, O’Neil’s orientations and Oliveira’s intentions have not allowed lasting continuity to be established. Strasbourg’s players constantly have to adapt, while collective automatisms are called into question.

The transfer window does not help matters. Strasbourg had a particularly busy summer, with a multitude of movements, including several players from the Chelsea ecosystem.

The club sometimes looks more like a piece in a vast player circulation system than one building its squad around clearly identified needs. Strasbourg’s sporting logic therefore seems regularly to come second to that of BlueCo.

It would be unfair, though, to deny the benefits of this policy: Strasbourg have rediscovered a European dimension and reached the semi-finals of the Conference League in spring 2026. The club also has a young squad with resale value, and has the resources to attract promising talent.

But what is the point of developing players if the best of them are liable to leave as soon as an opportunity arises within the group? What is the point of investing in a manager if he can be replaced so quickly?

Rosenior’s departures and the player movements between Strasbourg and Chelsea illustrate this difficulty in preserving a trajectory of the club’s own.

BlueCo has found in Alsace a tremendous breeding ground for its young talents. But Strasbourg cannot be reduced to a development centre at the service of Chelsea.

The French club’s supporters expect a team to identify with, a readable project and ambitions that do not change with the owner’s needs. By treating Strasbourg as an interchangeable element of its organisation, BlueCo risks weakening exactly what gives the club its value: its identity. Unless it is already too late? Strasbourg would benefit from disengaging from this stifling structure.

#1932. Man Utd fans tell Bryan Mbeumo to ‘go to sleep’ after posting GTA 6 photo

Manchester United fans have told Bryan Mbeumo to "go to bed" after the striker suggested he was playing GTA 6 ahead of Mauricio Pochettino first training session as manager.

A new era began at Man Utd on Wednesday with Pochettino's first day in charge, having flown in overnight following his final match as head coach of the USMNT.

Pochettino will take charge of first-team training for the first time on Thursday, with a daunting trip to Anfield to face Liverpool first up for the Argentine.

Full focus will be on making a positive start at the home of Man Utd's biggest rivals, but Mbeumo seemingly had something else top of his agenda on Wednesday evening.

A known video game fan, Mbeumo was one of thousands across the UK on Wednesday downloading the new GTA game ahead of its midnight launch.

Mbeumo posted an image of him close to 12am set to play what many are calling one of the greatest video games of all time.

And it did not go down too well with some Man Utd fans online.

One fan wrote: "So we're sat in the relegation zone, got a must-win match against our biggest rivals at the weekend, new gaffer's just flown in from America and bloody Mbeumo is up past midnight playing grand theft auto six."

“Doing a GTA all nighter the day before his 1st training session with a new manager is definitely a choice,” read another post.

Another fan posted "you have training tomorrow go to bed lol", while a third added: "We’re 18th and we play Liverpool next."

Ryan posted: "These lads have got to read the room and be a bit smarter with what they post."

Grant Dalgleish added, with angry emojis: "He’s got training in the morning!!!!"

There is no suggestion for long, if at all, Mbeumo played the game ahead of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday morning.

#1931. Mauricio Pochettino drops big tactics hint in first interview as Manchester United manager

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Mauricio Pochettino says he wants the Manchester United squad to feel "free" when playing in the new manager's first hint at his tactical approach.

Pochettino arrived at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday and on Thursday took charge of his first training session. On Sunday comes his first game, away at Anfield against Liverpool.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be tasked with dragging Man Utd out of the relegation zone and back into the top echelons of English football.

The now-sacked Michael Carrick oversaw the club's worst start to a season in 40 years, and much of the malaise was put down to his tactical setups and a lack of energy from the players on the pitch.

And Pochettino, who is known for his hard drills in training, wants to bring the energy back to his players.

“It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,” Pochettino told the club's official website.

“Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

We need to love the players that we have, we need to support the players

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

On the significance of culture to success, he adds: “To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

“We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.”

#1930. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Manchester United fans in first interview as manager

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a message to Manchester United fans in his first interview as manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has replaced the sacked Michael Carrick, and flew in from the United States on Wednesday morning to begin his two-and-a-half-year contract.

Pochettino on Thursday oversaw his first training session as head coach, and has a quick turnaround before his first game in charge - which comes on Sunday at Anfield to face Liverpool.

The Argentine is aware he faces a baptism of fire at the home of a rival this weekend, and hopes to earn his connection with the fans by playing with "fight" and "for the win".

The fans need to see that we are going to fight ... and we are going to play for the win

"I don't want to ask nothing because I think always we demand, demand, demand to the fans, but we need to provide to the fans before we demand," he told the club's official website.

"I think we need to be the next to connect. We need to be the part that we create that energy that connect to the fans, to provide the fans.

"The fans need to see that we are going to fight, that we are Manchester United and we respect our history and we are going to play for the win. And for sure then our fans will be supporting us because what I hear and what I saw in the past, the supporters are amazing."

He continued: “I know very well what that game means and how important it is. The history talks for us and to what we need to expect.

“We need to make sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

Aston Villa have reportedly identified AC Milan midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek as a potential winter transfer target.

Earlier on Wednesday, Villa announced that one of their current engine-room options had penned a new long-term contract.

Unai Emery is also not short of players for that position, with Boubacar Kamara, Joao Gomes, Leon Goretzka and Ross Barkley earning regular minutes.

Nevertheless, not helped by the inconsistent performances and individual mistakes of some of those aforementioned players, Villa remain off the pace in the Premier League.

According to Calciomercato, Loftus-Cheek has emerged as a possible option for the turn of the year.

The report alleges that Villa Park is viewed as a 'potential destination' for the former Chelsea midfielder.

Loftus-Cheek contributed 13 goals and 18 assists from his 155 appearances in a Blues shirt, but he has been at San Siro since the summer of 2023.

His stint at AC Milan can be viewed as a relative success, with 13 goals and four assists coming from 109 outings for the Italian giants.

However, the 11-cap England international's contract is due to expire at the end of the season, putting him in a position where he could leave on a free transfer in the summer.

Milan are open to cashing in on the 30-year-old in order to free up transfer funds and space on their wage bill.

Ruben Amorim's side have also won their last two matches against Inter Milan and Genoa, games which Loftus-Cheek missed through injury.

Despite Loftus-Cheek possessing qualities that Emery arguably lacks within his squad, a move to Villa makes little sense for the player.

Villa already have too many options in the number six, eight and 10 positions in Emery's familiar 4-2-3-1 or 4-4-1-1 formations.

Although Tammy Abraham has been linked with an exit from Villa, it seems unlikely that Loftus-Cheek would transition into a backup number nine behind Nicolas Jackson and Brian Madjo at this point of his career.

#1928. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final?

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents was revealed on Tuesday night as Norway produced a stunning comeback from 2-0 down pip Denmark to the runners-up spot behind Portugal in Group A4 by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1927. Prediction: Chelsea vs Leeds United

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon aiming to bounce back from a disappointing defeat before the international break when they host Leeds United in the Premier League.

The two clubs already served up an entertaining encounter earlier this season, with Chelsea coming from behind to secure a dramatic 6-3 victory in the EFL Cup. This latest meeting could prove equally important, as only two points separate the sides in the league table.

Chelsea entered the international break with renewed questions to answer after a mixed run of results under Xabi Alonso.

The Blues had recovered from a surprise home defeat to Tottenham Hotspur by beating Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, only to suffer a disappointing loss away to Sunderland in their final match before the break.

Alonso’s side have collected five wins, one draw and four defeats from their opening 10 Premier League fixtures, leaving them fifth in the table. While they remain firmly in the hunt for a top-four finish, the race is becoming increasingly congested, with just three points separating Chelsea from 10th-placed Aston Villa.

As veteran midfielder Jordan Henderson pointed out, consistency will be the key for the Blues’ prospects between now and the end of the season.

A return to Stamford Bridge should provide encouragement. Chelsea have accumulated 10 of their 16 league points at home and have scored 13 goals in front of their own supporters, the second-highest home tally in the division.

The Blues also boast an impressive recent record against Leeds on home soil, winning eight of their last 10 meetings at Stamford Bridge across all competitions. However, they were held to a 2-2 draw in this fixture last season after surrendering a two-goal advantage.

Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Jamie Gittens remain unavailable through injury.

There is hope that Joao Pedro could return after missing the last four matches due to a thigh problem, while Moises Caicedo, Jorrel Hato and Josh Acheampong are all fitness doubts.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is expected to return after recovering from a broken jaw and representing Argentina during the international break.

Morgan Rogers was one of Chelsea’s standout performers in the EFL Cup victory over Leeds, providing four assists, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both scored twice. However, Welbeck may start on the bench, with Alonso potentially favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central attacking role.

Leeds arrive in West London in significantly better spirits after ending a difficult spell before the international break.

Daniel Farke’s side had gone five matches without a victory before recording an important 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road. Noah Okafor’s late strike secured all three points and lifted Leeds into ninth place, just two points behind Chelsea.

The victory continued an encouraging home run, but Leeds have found life much tougher away from Elland Road. They have won only one of their last eight league fixtures on their travels, drawing four and losing three.

A demanding sequence of away matches now awaits, with trips to Chelsea, Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa on the horizon.

There are reasons for optimism, though. Leeds are unbeaten in their last two league meetings with Chelsea, following up a 3-1 home victory with a 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge. They now have the chance to go three consecutive league games without defeat against the Blues for the first time since 2001.

Speaking to the press ahead of the game, Farke was full of praise for the quality in Chelsea’s ranks.

Mateo Joseph continues to recover from a serious knee injury and remains unavailable.

Anton Stach is a doubt after missing the victory over Tottenham with a broken toe.

Farke could continue with a front two consisting of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, while Ethan Ampadu is expected to feature in midfield.

Noah Okafor will be pushing for a starting role after scoring from the bench against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are all contenders to return to the lineup.

Chelsea’s recent performances have lacked consistency, and the potential absence of a natural focal point in attack has reduced their threat in front of goal.

Leeds arrive with renewed confidence after their victory over Tottenham and have shown in recent meetings that they can cause problems for the Blues. However, their away form remains a concern, particularly against a Chelsea side that generally performs much better at Stamford Bridge.

It should be a close contest, but Chelsea’s superior attacking quality and strong home record give them the edge.

#1926. Nations League quarter-final draw simulated: England get favourable tie as Spain handed France rematch

The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals is now just days away, and England's route to potential international glory will become clearer.

Following the conclusion of an exciting and unpredictable group phase, the stage has been set as seven teams aim to dethrone two-time winners Portugal next summer.

The holders are safely through to the knockout phase as group winners, but they only confirmed their position on the final matchday after beating Wales in a five-goal thriller in Cardiff.

Joining Portugal in progressing from Group A4 are Norway following a remarkable comeback against Denmark on Tuesday night.

Trailing 2-0 after just 14 minutes, a brace from Erling Haaland and Martin Odegaard gave the World Cup quarter-finalists a 3-2 win as they pipped the Danes to the runners-up spot by virtue of a superior head-to-head record.

There was also final matchday drama in England’s group. Thomas Tuchel’s side travelled to Madrid needing to beat reigning world and European champions Spain to top Group A3 and did exactly that, despite playing the last half hour with 10-men.

Netherlands lost out on top spot to Germany in Group A2 after being thumped 5-0 by Jurgen Klopp’s side, but squeezed through on goal difference having finished level on points with Greece.

France and Belgium have qualified from Group A1, meaning seven of the top 11 ranked teams in the world have made it through to the Nations League quarter-finals.

So ahead of Friday's draw, who will be paired with who? Well, the four seeded sides each have three possibilities as teams from the same group cannot be paired with each other.

As a result, a knockout stage simulator has determined their potential opponents in the quarter-final and it's safe to say the results are quite fascinating.

In this simulation, England have been paired with the Netherlands in what would be a repeat of the semi-final during the inaugural season of the Nations League.

#1925. AFCON 2027: The nine countries already qualified for the tournament

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 12:59

The first qualified teams for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. The tournament is scheduled for 19 June to 17 July 2027 in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

With four of the six qualifying matchdays played, nine of the 24 qualified nations for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations are already known. Here are all the countries that have qualified.

After the three host nations, who qualify automatically although they are taking part in the qualifiers, the fourth matchday of the 2027 qualifying campaign revealed six new qualified teams on 17 November 2026.

The co-host of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is having a very mixed qualifying campaign. Benni McCarthy’s side did snatch a good point in South Africa (2-2), but they have only two points after four matchdays and had a scare at home against modest Eritrea (1-1).

Of the three host nations, Uganda are undoubtedly the ones having the best qualifying campaign, and the only ones to have won a match, a 1-0 victory over Libya. They are unbeaten after four matchdays and top their group ahead of Libya, Botswana and Tunisia.

The last of these automatically qualified nations, Tanzania have not necessarily made a strong impression. They have only two points after four matchdays, but they have just held Nigeria to a 0-0 draw, their best performance of the campaign so far.

One by one, the spots are being claimed! Here's who's qualified for #TotalEnergiesAFCON2027 after Matchday 4. ? https://t.co/uUJmkEBOVX

While waiting for the Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule on their status as 2025 champions or finalists, Senegal became the first team to secure their place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations on the pitch. After a laboured start in Mozambique (1-1), Patrick Vieira’s side strung together three wins, over Ethiopia and then Sudan twice, to confirm their ticket 24 hours after their matchday four game, thanks to a favourable result for Mozambique.

Held by Benin (1-1) in their opening game, Burkina Faso, round of 16 finalists in the last two editions, then dropped no more points, beating Central African Republic and then Mauritania twice. Amir Abdou’s side needed only four matchdays to qualify.

Round of 16 finalists in 2025, Benin will be present again for the Pamoja edition. After taking a good point from their trip to Burkina Faso (1-1), Gernot Rohr’s side dictated terms to Mauritania and then Central African Republic twice to secure qualification in November 2026, following Burkina Faso’s win over Mauritania.

After reaching the quarter-finals of the previous edition, Cameroon are taking these qualifiers very seriously. Held only in Congo, David Pagou’s side beat Comoros and Namibia twice to qualify after four matchdays, following Congo’s 1-0 defeat to Comoros.

Keen to go further than the quarter-finals, the ceiling reached in the last two editions, Mali confirmed their ambitions by being the only team along with Morocco to maintain a perfect record after four matchdays. World Cup-bound Cape Verde, Liberia and Rwanda twice all fell to Anthony Da Silva’s side, who qualified thanks to these wins.

As formidable as ever in these qualifiers, Morocco have a perfect 4/4 record, having beaten Gabon, Lesotho and then Niger twice. It was the second win over Niger, 1-0, thanks to a record-breaking goal from Abdellah Ouazane, that allowed Mohamed Ouahbi’s side to qualify.

#1923. Majority of clubs vote for extra legal protection for Premier League chiefs

Premier League board members have been given extra legal protection amid the threat of actions linked to the Manchester City case.

Eighteen clubs are reported to have supported changes to the league’s articles at a clubs meeting in central London on Thursday, which extend protections provided to individual board members to enable them to freely carry out their duties.

A 14-club majority is required for votes to be carried, and it was understood to have been comfortably above that.

The change comes after City sponsor Etihad said in September it was considering legal action over the “damaging” implications of the independent commission’s guilty verdict against the club.

The airline was not named in the verdict, which found City had benefited from “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and disguise costs to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules. City have appealed against the verdict. Another City sponsor, Etisalat, was reported by The Times to be considering similar action earlier this week.

The Press Association understands the issue was brought to a vote in order to bring the league’s individual legal cover in line with similar companies – including many of its clubs – and that these articles had not been looked at since the league’s inception in 1992.

There was no indication of any cap on the costs clubs could be exposed to as a result of the change to the league’s articles, and no wider discussion or questions raised on the City case despite this being the first shareholders’ meeting since the verdict was published on September 29.

Club executives also received a first update of the season from referees’ chief Howard Webb.

He is understood to have accepted the 10th round of matches immediately before the November international break had been especially difficult.

Six on-field errors were identified by the Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel which were not corrected by VAR intervention.

This is in part due to the high bar for intervention being operated this season, where referee’s on-field calls can only be overturned where it is felt the error was not a clear and obvious one.

#1922. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton and Hove Albion Verbruggen; Wieffer, Vuskovic, Boscagli, Dunk; Gross, Ayari; Gomez, Hinshelwood, De Cuyper; Rutter

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Aston Villa Bizot; Cash, Torres, Lindelof, Maatsen; Barkley, Kamara; McGinn, Gomes, Hemmings; Buendia

Subs Suzuki, Mings, Ruggeri, Bogarde, Alysson, Rowe, Burrowes, Garnacho, Lynch

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Reis, Kovacic, Cherki, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush

Bournemouth Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Cook, Scott; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#1921. Man City XI vs Fulham: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

Premier League football will soon resume after the international break, with Manchester City hoping to rectify their recent troubles against Fulham in Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

Since suffering their first loss of the Premier League season to Aston Villa, City have fallen to two further defeats at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

With time to think over the international break, Enzo Maresca has decisions to make when it comes to his starting XI for the visit of Fulham to the Etihad this weekend.

Marc Guehi missed international duty with England after coming off with an issue against Nottingham Forest, while Antoine Semenyo is a long-term absentee with a knee issue.

Abdukodir Khusanov was another to pull out from international duty after picking a knock against Forest.

In goal, Gianluigi Donnarumma has come under fire for his performances, but it seems unlikely that Maresca would drop the Italian international just yet.

With Guehi and Khusanov doubts, it makes sense to predict a centre-back pairing of Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol. Left back Nico O’Reilly is returning to both form and favour with Maresca, while Matheus Nunes is first choice on the opposite flank.

Enzo Fernandez is definitely a favourite of Maresca, and while the Argentine travelled to South America to play two friendlies with his national side, he was rested for 35 minutes in the second game.

Elliott Anderson received a similar amount of rest while away with England - coming off early during their 3-2 victory over Spain courtesy of a red card.

City paid over £250million to overhaul their midfield this summer, and the duo’s quality should see them start.

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Phil Foden was dropped for the defeat to Forest, but City’s performance might encourage Maresca to restore the England international to the starting XI. In order to fit both Foden and Rayan Cherki into the side, the former will have to go on the right wing, with the latter playing centrally.

We’re predicting that Jeremy Doku will get the nod on the left - with Erling Haaland leading the line up top.

Predicted Man City XI vs Fulham (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

Date and time: 12.30pm GMT on Saturday, November 21

#1920. Richter: Sullivan ‘not afraid’ ahead of MLS playoffs

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Philadelphia Union interim head coach Ryan Richter is confident Cavan Sullivan will rise to the occasion in the MLS Cup Playoffs, as he has no fear.

Philadelphia finished sixth in the Eastern Conference, setting up a Round One best-of-three series against the New England Revolution.

Sullivan's form was key to the Union's mid-season turnaround as he spurred the team into a 14-game unbeaten run following the World Cup break, and he scored twice to help them secure a 4-1 win over Toronto FC on Decision Day.

And Richter believes the 17-year-old's fearlessness will be a huge help to the Union as they chase their first MLS Cup.

"The thing is, he has the personality for that," Richter told MLSsoccer.com.

"He has the mentality. He's not afraid of the moment. He's excited by it, and he has the personality to take the pressure that comes with that and perform.

"It's a lot of hard work that got him here. Of course he has the talent, he has the support system, and he has the personality, but he works very hard for everything that's coming to him."

The kid continues to shine Cavan Sullivan is a finalist for @MLS MVP and Young Player of the Year! https://t.co/2iCJei3d3i

— Philadelphia Union (@PhilaUnion) November 12, 2026

New England, meanwhile, finished third in the East, recording their best finish to a regular-season campaign since topping the charts in 2021.

They are playing in their first playoff campaign in three years, though they followed up a four-game winning run by losing their last two matches.

One boost is that Jack Harrison is closing in on a return, and he hopes he is able to do so in the playoffs.

"I think ultimately it's down to Marko [Mitrovic, head coach] and what the game is asking for," he told The Soccer Show.

"We have to be smart and strategic in the playoffs, with the first round being best of three. It's something to think about, but I'm definitely excited to potentially get some minutes at some point."

Carles Gil was the driving force behind New England qualifying for the playoffs, with 25 goal involvements (13 goals, 12 assists), at least six more than any other player (Dor Turgeman with 19).

Gil also topped the charts for chances created (95) and crosses (183), and his creativity will be key to sparking the Revs' attack.

The one and only Carles Gil is your 2026 Team MVP, as voted by the fans for a club-record sixth time overall. https://t.co/BAf4SSwogy

— New England Revolution (@NERevolution) November 19, 2026

Sullivan has been a revelation during his breakout season, and he signed off for the regular season with a brace against Toronto to take his goal tally to nine for the campaign.

He overperformed his expected goals by 2.0 (7.0 xG), but he was also stringing things together as well, with no Philadelphia player bettering his tally of 14 assists.

These sides met in the First Round of the Playoffs last time New England qualified back in 2023, and it was the Union who came out on top in the best-of-three series.

Philadelphia won the first game 3-1 at home and followed it up with a 1-0 victory at Gillette Stadium to book their place in the next round.

New England won both meetings with the Union in the regular season in 2026, winning 2-1 home and away. That followed a six-game losing streak against Philadelphia.

However, the Revs head into the postseason having lost their last two matches, though Philadelphia's win on Decision Day ended a four-game winless streak (D2 L2).
