#1919. Bayern Munich vs FC Koln - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 13:05

Bayern Munich can take a lead in the race for the Bundesliga title on Friday, when they welcome FC Koln to Allianz Arena.

The hosts are level on 21 points with second-placed Borussia Dortmund, who play on Saturday, whereas Koln are 15th with nine points after nine matchweeks.

Prior to the start of the November international break, Bayern emerged as 2-1 victors against Mainz 05, though they were wasteful in the final third, missing three of their four big chances while scoring just two of their 26 shots.

That win was their fourth in five games in all competitions, but it will be a concern that the team have only kept one clean sheet in their last eight matches.

The Bavarians have conceded 17 goals in their 16 fixtures this season, whereas they only conceded 13 times in the corresponding period in 2025-26.

Fans will hope the expected return of Vincent Kompany, who has not been in the dugout for his side's last five fixtures since collapsing on October 23, will help boost the team's performances at the back.

Bayern have drawn two of their three most recent contests at Allianz Arena, though they are yet to experience defeat at home, winning five of their seven clashes when playing as hosts.

Kompany's side have averaged five goals per game at home in the Bundesliga, while they only conceded four goals in their four league outings at Allianz Arena.

Koln were beaten 2-1 by Bayer Leverkusen on November 8 before the start of the international break, and it will concern supporters that the club have now won just one of their past eight top-flight games (W1, D4, L3).

Manager Rene Wagner will want his team to improve considerably in the final third given they have netted just twice in their last four league fixtures, blanking on two occasions.

A defeat on Friday would leave the visitors as low as 17th should Union Berlin and Schalke 04 claim three points in matchday 10, though it should be noted that only three points separate them from eighth-placed Stuttgart.

The Billy Goats' record against Bayern is predictably poor, with Wagner's side last beating their hosts in February 2011, and another loss would be their 22nd defeat in 24 meetings.

Koln's solitary victory in their five away matches this campaign came in the DFB-Pokal against Wurzburger Kickers in August, and they have since lost three games and settled for a stalemate once.

Bayern's injuries are still extensive despite the break from football, with left-back Alphonso Davies (hamstring) and goalkeeper Manuel Neuer (foot), as well as attackers Luis Diaz (hamstring) and Serge Gnabry (hamstring), among those to miss out.

Jonas Urbig will feature between the posts, while Josip Stanisic is almost certain to be stationed at left-back, with Dayot Upamecano and Jonathan Tah set to start as centre-backs.

In the forward line, Ballon d'or-winner Harry Kane may play ahead of a supporting cast consisting of Lennart Karl, Michael Olise and Nathaniel Brown.

Koln are also dealing with several injury issues, especially in defence considering both Timo Hubers and Rav van den Berg will be absent.

Joel Schmied, Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and Tom Krauss are the likely trio to start in the visitors' back three, while the club's attacking efforts will be led by forwards Marius Bulter and Said El Mala.

Urbig; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanisic; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Karl, Olise, Brown; Kane

Schwabe; Schmied, Simpson-Pusey, Krauss; Sebulonsen, Maina, Okon-Engstler, Johannesson, Sosa; Bulter, El Mala

Bayern Munich have shown that they are far from flawless at the back in recent months, so there should be openings for Koln.

However, the Bavarians have continued to be irresistible in attack despite their injuries, and they should be able to get the better of the visitors.

Andoni Iraola should have a relatively healthy squad to choose from when he selects Liverpool’s starting XI to face arch-rivals Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

The Reds are still waiting on the availability of club captain Virgil van Dijk and midfielder Ryan Gravenberch.

#1917. Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils set 'money aside' for £40m USA attacker

By Saikat Mandal | 18 Nov 2026 13:25

Manchester United have reportedly set aside funds to sign Monaco striker Folarin Balogun during the January transfer window.

The 25-year-old was one of the standout performers for the USA at the 2026 World Cup and was heavily linked with a move to Tottenham Hotspur during the summer window.

Balogun also came close to joining Everton for £40m in the summer, but the proposed move collapsed after he failed a medical in the closing stages of negotiations.

A potential January departure could now be on the cards, with Man Utd reportedly keen to bring the striker to Old Trafford.

Arresting the club's rapid decline should be Mauricio Pochettino's first priority, but the manager would also be keen to bring in players of his choosing in January to strengthen key areas of the squad.

Having coached Balogun at international level, the prospect of a reunion is an obvious one, while the striker's representatives are also actively exploring a potential switch from Monaco to Old Trafford.

According to Football Insider, signing a new striker is Manchester United's second priority, with Pochettino keen to strengthen other areas of the pitch first.

The Red Devils want to reinforce their defence before turning their attention to the attack, although they could pursue Balogun if funds remain available after addressing their defensive shortcomings.

Monaco are reportedly willing to offload Balogun, who has managed just one Ligue 1 goal in six appearances this season, all of which have come from the bench.

The former Arsenal striker has scored 32 goals in 98 appearances for Monaco across all competitions and could prove a smart addition for Man Utd.

The Red Devils, however, could face stiff competition from Serie A giants Juventus, who are reportedly exploring a potential swap deal involving Edon Zhegrova.

Balogun is said to be attracted by the prospect of moving to Turin, meaning United could face a significant battle for his signature if they are serious about securing his services.

#1916. Injured Manchester United pair spotted in training as Mauricio Pochettino leads first session

Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu both shook off injury concerns to take part in Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager on Thursday.

Pochettino has been thrown in at the deep end with United. He joins a club sitting 18th in the Premier League, and must visit Liverpool in his first match this weekend.

His predecessor, Michael Carrick, was beset by a number of frustrating injuries in the latter stages of his tenure, but Pochettino is hoping to welcome a number of absentees back into the fold this weekend.

And it has been confirmed that both Maguire and Dorgu are back in training ahead of the fated visit to Anfield.

Maguire was a doubt for the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa before the international break and was fortunate to start, but only lasted 45 minutes before being forced off with a back spasm. Dorgu returned from injury to feature off the bench in that match, but was not considered fit enough to represent Denmark during the international break.

But the fact both have returned to training suggests they will be fit for Sunday’s trip across the north-west, with United confirming they took part in the full session.

United have released a slate of pictures from Pochettino’s first session, showing the Argentine getting to know the likes of Leny Yoro and Bryan Mbeumo.

Elsewhere, Lisandro Martinez will be available having served a suspension imposed after he was sent off at Stamford Bridge on Halloween.

Pochettino will also hope to be able to call upon longer-term absentees Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford this weekend, with some reports suggesting they will finally be ready to return from muscle and hip problems, respectively. It is unclear whether either man trained on Thursday.

Pochettino will deliver a more detailed team news update when he faces the media for the first time as United boss on Friday afternoon.

#1914. Thomas Frank confirms Chelsea man ‘very close’ to becoming his first Crystal Palace signing

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Thomas Frank has confirmed Crystal Palace are working to appoint Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, with a deal “very close.”

Frank was appointed the Eagles’ head coach this week, replacing the Frenchman Pierre Sage, who lasted just 16 matches in the job and left the club dead last in the Premier League.

As he looks to establish his coaching staff, though, Frank is looking into a reunion with Cueva. The pair were colleagues at Brentford between 2020 and 2024, when Cueva was poached by the Blues, who reportedly spent £1m to secure his services.

But Chelsea have upgraded on Cueva this season, signing Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee in a similarly pricey move.

Palace have reportedly been in talks with Chelsea over Cueva’s transfer for some time, and Frank, speaking in his first press conference since taking over, has now confirmed the widespread reports that a deal is imminent.

He said Cueva is “very close” to joining his staff. He is expected to serve as a general assistant coach, rather than as a dedicated set-piece coach.

Frank’s backroom staff is currently comprised of Paddy McCarty and Andy Quy, with BBC Sport reporting Palace are working to add Justin Cochrane and Chris Haslam, both of whom have worked with the Dane in previous posts.

Top of Frank’s to-do list in south-east London is to rectify Palace’s form and drag them out of the relegation zone, with a trip to Coventry on the cards this weekend.

"I know it'll be difficult,” said Frank of Saturday’s match. "But I also trust the boys, I know we'll perform on Saturday. We just need a little margin to go in our favour."

The quality of Palace’s summer recruitment has been criticised this season and cited by some as a reason for Sage’s struggles.

But Frank insisted he has plenty to work with as he looks to get the club back on track: "I'm looking forward to come in to do everything I can to help the team, the club.

#1913. ‘I’m very healthy’ – Kompany returning to the dugout when Bayern host Koln

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vincent Kompany will return to the touchline for the first time since October, when Bayern Munich host Koln in the Bundesliga on Friday.

Kompany has been recuperating after being taken to hospital following a collapse at the club’s training ground last month. He was subsequently diagnosed with meningeal irritation.

In his absence, Bayern have continued their strong start to the season and sit top of the table after nine games with 21 points (W6 D3).

They went into the international break on the back of a 2-1 win over Mainz, and they are looking to move clear of Borussia Dortmund before the rest of the weekend's action.

"It was very intense," he said. "At the time, it was a new experience.

"Looking back, everything went perfectly. I received support right away from the club and the doctors. I'm very grateful.

"You try to stay calm and wait until you have the results. It was a positive process; all the tests were positive.

"I have to say, I'm very healthy. We did a lot of tests, and they all came back fine. In those quiet moments, you also try to learn.

"Now I feel very good again, and I'm happy to be back with the team."

All smiles ahead of tomorrow! https://t.co/hDRW2I2MSx

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 19, 2026

While Bayern are enjoying an unbeaten start to the season, Koln are sat down in 15th, having accumulated just nine points so far.

They are winless in their last four matches (D2 L2), but no matter what, Kompany is relishing the contest.

"There's one person at Bayern who is really motivated for this game against Koln. I've been waiting for four weeks," he said.

"It wasn't difficult to get myself in the right frame of mind. I've had plenty of time. Motivation is always high for every match, and it certainly is for this one.

"I hope I can convey that to the team. They're just back from international duty. It's a Friday game, so anything can happen. If the players can sense my motivation, we'll have a good foundation for the match."

Kane has failed to score in his last four matches in all competitions, his joint-longest goal drought for Bayern.

However, he has already provided eight assists in the Bundesliga this season, a new record for a player after nine matchdays since Opta began recording this data in 2004-05 and already equalling his personal record for a single Bundesliga season (also 2023-24 and 2024-25).

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 19, 2026

El Mala recently scored his 16th Bundesliga goal for Koln; only Dieter Muller (32) and Lukas Podolski (22) scored more Bundesliga goals for the club before their 21st birthday.

Among all U21 players in Europe's big-five leagues since the start of last season, only Barcelona's Lamine Yamal (26) has scored more goals than El Mala (16).

Bayern have not lost any of their last 22 Bundesliga matches against Koln (W20 D2) since a 2-3 away defeat in February 2011.

Among current Bundesliga teams, Bayern only have a longer unbeaten run against Schalke (24 matches).

Indeed, Bayern are the only team from Europe's big-five leagues to remain unbeaten in all competitions this season (W11 D5). They have lost only one of their last 41 matches in all competitions across two seasons, a 4-5 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League semi-final first leg in late April.

Of all teams to have played continuously in the Bundesliga since the start of last season, Koln have won the fewest points over the last 34 matchdays (27), while Bayern have won the most (83).

Over the last eight matchdays, only Borussia Monchengladbach have won fewer points (four) than Koln (six).

Koln are also winless in their last 17 Bundesliga away games (D7 L10), the longest current run of any team in the competition and equalling their negative club record set in 2003-04.

#1912. Man United transfer news: Five USA players who could follow Mauricio Pochettino to Old Trafford including teenage star

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 13:51, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 13:54

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has suggested that he could potentially target USA players in the upcoming transfer windows.

Pochettino has left his role with the United States to take charge of Man United, with the Argentine now in England preparing for Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool.

There has been a host of speculation in recent days surrounding potential USA arrivals at Man United, and here Sports Mole looks at five possible recruits for the 20-time English champions from the Stars and Stripes.

Man United need a striker due to Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems, and Balogun is currently being linked with a potential switch to Old Trafford.

The 25-year-old has scored 32 goals and registered 13 assists in 98 appearances for Monaco, while he has a record of 13 goals in 33 caps for USA.

Balogun's career started at Arsenal, but he only managed two goals in 10 appearances for the London club's first team before leaving in search of pastures new.

The United States international has since developed into an impressive forward, and a move to Man United during the January transfer window is thought to be possible.

Man United will overhaul their defence in 2027, and Freeman is believed to be very much on the club's radar, with that link growing since it was confirmed that Pochettino would be arriving.

Freeman, 22, made the move to Villarreal from Orlando City in January 2026, and he has scored once in 25 appearances for the Yellow Submarine.

The right-back has now been capped on 28 occasions by the USA, and there is a belief that he could secure a move to a major club in the not too distant future.

Man United are expected to sign at least two new full-backs next year, and one of those could potentially be Freeman, who has hugely impressed since his arrival in Spain.

Man United were linked with Adams long before Pochettino arrived, with the club thought to have considered moving for the USA international during the recent transfer window.

The 27-year-old has been capped on 64 occasions by his country and has featured on 77 occasions for Bournemouth, scoring three goals and registering seven assists.

Adams has actually now made 90 career appearances in the Premier League, including his time at Leeds United, and his high-energy style has attracted a host of attention.

The midfielder's contract at Bournemouth is due to expire in June 2028, and if a new deal is not agreed by next summer, there is expected to again be a lot of focus on his future.

McKennie has recently commented on claims that Man United could target USA players, and the 28-year-old is one of those to be linked with a move to Old Trafford.

The midfielder has experience of the Premier League, playing 19 times in the competition while on loan at Leeds United during the 2022-23 campaign.

McKennie has scored once and registered one assist in 11 appearances for Juventus this season, while he has played 73 times for his country.

The midfielder has made 241 appearances for Juventus, scoring 28 goals and registering 28 assists, and it would not be a shock to see him make the move to Old Trafford.

Hall has made a flying start to his senior career with the USA, scoring five times in six appearances, while the 18-year-old has 20 goals and six assists in 79 appearances for New York Red Bulls.

The teenager was on the scoresheet in both matches against Haiti ahead of Pochettino's exit, and a number of major clubs are believed to be keeping a close eye on his situation.

Should Hall continue to find the back of the net at an impressive rate, then a dream move to Man United could potentially be on the cards in the not too distant future.

#1910. Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session hit by concerning security breach

Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.

The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his new club.

With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.

But his preparations for that match have already been compromised in a concerning security breach at United’s training centre, after a drone secretly recorded 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first session with the club, with footage posted on YouTube for all to see.

The drone does not appear to have entered Carrington’s airspace at any point, but footage filmed with a zoom lens shows the session in clear detail.

The YouTube channel which posted the clip followed it up with a statement claiming they had broken no laws by recording the session as the airspace around Carrington is unrestricted.

No players or staff caught in the footage appeared to be aware of the fact they were being filmed. At the time of writing, the clip has accrued over 40,000 views.

The footage shows the United squad working in two groups. One was being put through a rondo on one pitch, while Pochettino led the other through what appeared to be a tactical session on another. Both groups appeared to comprise a blend of first-team and academy players.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Standard Sport.

Fulham are in talks with captain Calvin Bassey over a new contract as they look to fend off interest from Manchester United.

The 26-year-old centre-back, whose contract expires next summer, is understood to be on United’s shortlist as they look to sign defensive reinforcements in January.

Fulham hold the option to extend Bassey’s current deal by a further year.

The Cottagers are keen to keep hold of Bassey, especially after Alvaro Arbeloa promoted him to captain in the summer.

Nothing has been agreed yet, but Fulham have opened talks with Bassey over a new contract and do not intend to sell him in January.

The Nigerian international has played every minute of Fulham’s league campaign so far this season, and is viewed as an integral part of Arbeloa’s plans.

After failing to win any of their first six league games this term, Fulham have taken eight points from their last four matches, moving two points clear of the relegation zone.

Over that four-game period, Fulham kept two clean sheets and conceded just two goals, with Bassey at the heart of defence.

They are therefore determined to fend off any interest in Bassey by tying him down to a new long-term deal.

United, meanwhile, are expected to be active in the January transfer market, with Mauricio Pochettino identifying centre-back as a priority position for the Red Devils.

His current centre-back options include Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez, and the youngsters Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.

Martinez will also be out of contract this summer, and his future remains up in the air.

#1906. Gross a Brighton ‘legend’, says team-mate Chema

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Brighton's Chema Andres has hailed Pascal Gross as a club legend ahead of the playmaker's potential milestone appearance.

Gross' next game will be his 300th appearance for Brighton, who he originally joined in 2017.

The 35-year-old left Brighton for Borussia Dortmund in 2024, but returned to the Seagulls in January and has been a standout performer this season.

Fabian Hurzeler's team sit in second in the Premier League, and Gross has been crucial.

Gross has created 29 chances in the top-flight this term, more than any other player in the competition. He has been directly involved in eight goals, which is a tally bettered by only Erling Haaland and Evanilson (both nine).

And fellow midfielder Chema sees the German as the ideal role model.

"Since day one [at Brighton], I've always watched him train every day," Andres told Brighton's media channels.

"What are his habits, what is he doing, what is he not doing? That is also really important. But the way he treats people, especially young people like me, I think is the thing that surprised me when I came here.

"How he tries to help us, how he tries to give us advice and everything else, because I think he has a lot of experience. He's a legend here in the club, and, of course, I try to listen and learn a lot from him."

Brighton will be out to continue their fantastic form when they face Hull City on Sunday.

It marks the first ever top-flight meeting between Hull and Brighton, and the first in any competition since a goalless draw in the Championship in February 2016.

Only Elliot Anderson has won more duels (74) than McBurnie in the Premier League this season (71).

McBurnie's 41 aerial duels won are third among strikers, behind Thierno Barry (45) and Dominic Calvert-Lewin (43).

Gross' goal against Brentford for Brighton last time out was his 87th Premier League goal involvement (35 goals, 52 assists), the joint-most by a German in the competition (level with Mesut Ozil).

The Brighton man leads the 2026-27 Premier League for chances created overall (29) and in open play (23).

Opta's supercomputer has the Seagulls as the favourites, but Brighton are winless in all six of their visits to MKM Stadium in all competitions (D2 L4). Their last away win against Hull came at Boothferry Park in the fourth tier in October 2000.

Hull won their first two Premier League games this season but are winless in all eight since then (D5 L3). It is the fourth time a side has won their first two games, then none of their next eight in the competition, along with Wolves in 2011-12, Hull in 2016-17, and West Brom in 2017-18, all of whom were relegated.

Their eight-game winless run is the longest in the Premier League this term, along with Manchester United.

Brighton have been leading for 54.3% of their Premier League games this season, the highest ratio of any side.

They have also scored a league-high 15 goals while already leading in the competition this term, and are one of just three sides yet to concede a goal while ahead in 2026-27 (also Arsenal and Sunderland).

Hull rank bottom of the Premier League this season for shots (103), touches in the opponent’s box (182), and expected goals (9.5), while Brighton are second for shots (169) and xG (19.4).

#1905. Real Madrid star Arda Guler rewarded for what is set to be his best campaign yet

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:06, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 15:07

Real Madrid have announced that Arda Guler has signed a new contract at Bernabeu until the end of the 2031-32 campaign.

The Turkey international made the move to Bernabeu from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, and he has represented the capital giants on 126 occasions, scoring 22 goals and registering 32 assists in the process.

Guler has started the campaign with four goals and seven assists in 14 appearances in all competitions, including three goals and five assists in 12 La Liga outings.

Real Madrid have announced that the 21-year-old has agreed a new deal in the Spanish capital until the summer of 2032.

"Real Madrid C. F. and Arda Guler have agreed to extend the contract of our player, who will remain linked to the club until June 30, 2032," read a statement from the capital giants.

Guler has started 10 of Real Madrid's 12 La Liga matches this season, demonstrating his importance for Los Blancos, although he has only played in two of their four Champions League league stage fixtures this term.

The playmaker missed the team's 2026-27 European opener against Inter Milan through suspension, while he was rested against AEK Athens in their last game in the competition.

Guler has not scored more than six times in a campaign for Real Madrid since his arrival, but he is already just two goals off that total in November.

Real Madrid won La Liga and the Champions League during Guler's first campaign at the club, but he only featured on 12 occasions in 2023-24.

Guler has won five trophies during his time at Bernabeu, but this could be his best campaign yet both from a personal and team point of view.

Guler is expected to be in the starting team when Real Madrid continue their La Liga campaign against Celta Vigo on November 21.

The playmaker will then be hoping to make his third Champions League appearance of the season when Los Blancos face PSV Eindhoven in the competition on November 24.

#1904. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the eight teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position was Group A4 was confirmed after their win over Wales on Tuesday, though it is Norway joining them in the knockout phases following a remarkable comeback win against Denmark.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

Pot 1: France, England, Germany, Portugal

Pot 2: Belgium, Spain, Netherlands, Norway

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

The first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The final tournament is scheduled for June 2027.

#1903. Who can England face in Nations League draw? Dream and nightmare scenario revealed

England will learn their opponents for the Nations League quarter-finals on Friday morning.

The Three Lions beat Spain in dramatic circumstances in Madrid to top their group last week, and can now avoid the likes of France, Germany and Portugal in the quarter-finals as a result.

But the draw might still throw up some tricky fixtures as England look to improve on their best-ever finish in this competition, which came when they crossed the line in third in 2019.

Here is all you need to know about their potential opponents...

England are in Pot 1 for the Nations League draw, along with France, Germany and Portugal.

The teams in Pot 2 are Belgium, Spain, the Netherlands and Norway.

The Nations League draw will pit each of the four teams in Pot 1 against one of those in Pot 2, for a two-legged quarter-final.

There is one provision, though: teams from the same group cannot be drawn against each other, meaning England cannot face Spain at this stage of the competition. They could, however, come across them in the semi-finals or final.

As such, England could draw Belgium, the Netherlands, or Norway in the quarter-final.

Semi-final matchups will be determined by another draw following the quarter-finals.

England’s dream opponent at this stage of the Nations League is Norway.

FIFA sees Martin Odegaard and Erling Haaland’s side as comfortably the lowest-ranked of England’s three potential opponents.

That is in spite of their impressive World Cup campaign - where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by England - and the fact they turned over both Denmark and Wales in the November international break.

England’s nightmare draw, meanwhile, would see them pitted against Belgium.

It is tough to say whether Belgium or the Netherlands would be the tougher opponent at this stage - FIFA ranks them at eighth and ninth in the world, respectively - but the Red Devils just pip their neighbours.

They finished second in their group, just a single point off winners France. A pair of one-sided victories over Turkiye and Italy got them to this stage.

The quarter-final first-legs are scheduled for March 25-27, with the return legs scheduled for March 28-30.

The semi-finals and final will be played in June 2027.

#1902. Leeds confirm huge injury boost for Chelsea clash as two stars return

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Daniel Farke expects to have Anton Stach in the squad when Leeds visit Chelsea on Saturday.

The Blues have only won one of their last three league outings, with defeats by Sunderland and Tottenham coming either side of a 2-0 victory over Manchester United, but have their work cut out for them if they are to get back to winning ways sa they host Farke’s Leeds.

But Farke has hinted his countryman will be back in the fold for the trip to Stamford Bridge, having spent the past week training with his team-mates.

"Dominic [Calvert-Lewin], since he came back from England duties, is also back in training and no problems, so definitely good news."

That leaves Farke with a fully-fit squad for the trip down to west London, a considerable boost for his chances. of picking up three points.

Chelsea, meanwhile, remain injury-hit. It is not yet clear whether Joao Pedro will be available to return from his own injury, while Moises Caicedo has also picked up an issue on international duty.

Reece James is in recovery from knee surgery, with centre-back Maxence Lacroix also out until the new year.

#1901. Antonio Rudiger compares Kylian Mbappe to Cristiano Ronaldo in Real Madrid defence

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 15:20

Real Madrid defender Antonio Rudiger has launched a passionate defence of Kylian Mbappe's contribution to the team, drawing a striking comparison with Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and Gareth Bale to challenge criticism of the Frenchman's defensive work.

Mbappe has been one of Madrid's most prolific players since arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024, reaching 100 goals for the Spanish giants despite their struggles to win major silverware over the past two seasons.

However, his extraordinary goalscoring record has not prevented questions being raised about his willingness to press opponents and contribute when Madrid are out of possession.

The issue has become particularly prominent under Jose Mourinho, whose demanding approach requires his players to maintain their defensive organisation.

Rudiger believes some of those expectations are misplaced, arguing that a forward of Mbappe's quality should be judged primarily on his ability to decide matches.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with The Athletic, the former Chelsea centre-back questioned whether it made sense to demand the same defensive responsibilities from a player who has already delivered 100 goals for Madrid.

"Should I tell Mbappe [...] to do my job? It makes no sense," Rudiger said.

The German then pointed to one of the most successful attacking partnerships in Real Madrid's history to explain his position.

Rudiger believes Madrid's previous success offers an important lesson about how to accommodate outstanding attacking players.

He recalled the celebrated partnership of Ronaldo, Bale and Benzema, who spearheaded the club's attack during a period that produced four Champions League titles between 2014 and 2018.

The trio were renowned for their individual attacking qualities and ability to deliver decisive moments in major matches.

Rudiger suggested that Madrid did not achieve those successes by constantly scrutinising their forwards' defensive contributions.

He pointed to the achievements of the three players before insisting that discussion of attackers should not always revolve around their work without the ball.

His argument is particularly relevant to Mbappe, whose goals have frequently provided Madrid with a decisive advantage even when the team's collective performances have attracted criticism.

The French international has continued to deliver exceptional numbers in front of goal, although Madrid have struggled to translate his individual productivity into the trophies expected at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Rudiger's comments do not suggest that Mbappe should be exempt from defensive responsibilities. Rather, the defender believes the rest of the team must find an effective balance around players whose greatest value comes in attacking positions.

The comparison with Ronaldo is especially significant given the Portuguese forward's standing at Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 appearances and helped establish an era of sustained European dominance.

Mbappe has already been compared to Ronaldo following his spectacular individual performances for Madrid, but Rudiger has approached the comparison from a different perspective.

For the experienced defender, the question is how Madrid can create the conditions for their most influential attackers to flourish.

Rudiger also addressed another recurring criticism of Madrid's squad: the difficulty of managing a dressing room filled with established international stars.

The 33-year-old acknowledged that the club's collection of strong personalities can create challenges for any manager.

He referred to Rafael Benitez and Julen Lopetegui, whose spells in charge of Madrid ended prematurely, as examples of coaches who encountered similar difficulties.

"It's not a myth. That's the reality," Rudiger admitted when discussing the influence of big personalities at the club.

His comments offer an insight into the environment Mourinho has inherited since returning to Madrid during the summer.

The Portuguese manager has been tasked with restoring the club's success after two seasons without a major trophy, with Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior among the players expected to lead that recovery.

Rudiger spoke positively about Mourinho's influence, revealing that the manager had contacted him towards the end of last season to explain his plans and express his desire to keep the German at the club.

He also described a lighter side to Mourinho's personality, explaining that the former Manchester United and Chelsea boss enjoys telling jokes in the dressing room while maintaining a far more demanding approach on the training pitch.

The defender extended his support to Vinicius, who has experienced a difficult start to the season and faced increased competition for his position.

Rudiger insisted that the Brazilian continues to work hard to improve his performances and remains an important figure in Madrid's plans.

Vinicius has recently rediscovered his goalscoring form with Brazil, scoring five times across two international friendlies against Japan and Singapore.

His return presents Mourinho with another selection decision as Madrid prepare to resume their domestic campaign.

For Rudiger, however, the responsibility for restoring Madrid's success cannot rest solely on the willingness of Mbappe, Vinicius or Bellingham to defend.

His comparison with Ronaldo's celebrated attacking partnership reflects a broader conviction that Madrid must find a collective structure capable of making the most of their attacking talent.

#1900. Manchester United XI vs Liverpool: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

Mauricio Pochettino will pick his first Manchester United team on Sunday for a daunting debut away at Liverpool.

The Argentine was appointed Michael Carrick’s successor last week and only arrived in the north-west on Wednesday, leaving him just a handful of sessions to prepare his side for a crunch fixture.

As such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

Carlos Baleba remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained against Roma in the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko also out until the new year, but Pochettino may well be boosted by the returns of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw. The latter seems the more likely of the two, with Rashford yet to be pictured in training since the international break.

Pochettino is known to be very fond of Rashford, and has reportedly attempted to sign him to other teams he has managed, meaning he can expect to get the nod if fit.

Should fit-again Shaw slot in at left-back, he may do so as one of two fresh faces in the back four. Lisandro Martinez has served his red card suspension and will be available to partner Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot at right-back.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Patrick Dorgu is expected to be fit, too, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Matheus Cunha off the left. He could also deputise Shaw if his fitness levels are not up to par.

Leaked drone footage of United’s Thursday training session appeared to show Pochettino working on tactics with a tight-knit group of ten outfield players, leading some to speculate that he might be dealing with Sunday’s starters. The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks this, though, given neither has started a Premier League match this season.

#1899. Quill confident Dallas are ‘well-oiled machine’ for playoffs

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Eric Quill believes FC Dallas are a "well-oiled machine" going into the MLS Cup Playoffs and is excited to see what they can do in the first match of Round One against the Portland Timbers.

Dallas finished second in the Western Conference to ensure they had home advantage in the best-of-three series, having finished the regular season with just one loss in their last six games (W3 D2).

They recorded their best finish since 2016 when they topped the West, and they have qualified for the playoffs in back-to-back seasons, though they were knocked out in Round One last year.

Quill is confident Dallas can improve on that result, though, claiming the drop in temperatures will only play into his team's strength on the press.

"We are a well-oiled machine right now, as far as across the board, just guys, how bought in they are and how much they're up for this," Quill told MLSSoccer.com.

"And our team speed, our pressing ability, the change of weather going into the high 60s, low 70s, is only going to help our game model, because we want to press and be really proactive, front-footed.

"We're going to be on people from minute 1 to 95."

The stage is set Our Round One playoff schedule is locked in. https://t.co/bv1xI7bAdu

— X – FC Dallas (@FCDallas) November 8, 2026

Portland, meanwhile, just snuck into the automatic playoff spots due to a strong finish to the regular season.

They went unbeaten in their last five games, winning each of the last four (D1), including a 2-0 win over Austin FC on Decision Day, which meant they pipped the Seattle Sounders to seventh.

"When we look at the progress, there have been some improvements, but you need to be consistent in that," head coach Marti Cifuentes said.

"We have to learn to be ourselves, whatever the game scenario. If we start well, then we need to keep on our philosophy.

"But obviously there is an opposition as well. There is always an opponent that prepares well for the game, and that's why the game is so beautiful, because sometimes you just need to cope with the reality of the game.

"I would say we need to at our best in our key identity and principles of the game."

Joaquin Valiente got the scoring started for Dallas in their win over the Rapids on Decision Day, netting just his third goal of the season.

He has been an effective playmaker, though, with nobody on the team bettering his 13 assists, while he also topped the charts for crosses (115) and chances created (48).

Jimer Fory has helped keep the Timbers ticking throughout the season, with no Portland player registering more touches (2,016), interceptions (63) or possessions won (161).

Only Finn Surman (1,570) attempted more passes than the Colombian (1,437), but Fory was a solid presence at the back with more successful tackles (32/54) than anyone else.

Dialed in the details https://t.co/QpLaIlYwN0

— Portland Timbers (@TimbersFC) November 18, 2026

Dallas have never won a postseason clash with Portland in 90 minutes (D2 L2). They lost in the first round in both 2015 and 2018, but advanced in 2020 after winning on penalties.

Dallas are unbeaten in their last six regular-season matches against Portland (W3 D3), with all three victories coming on home soil. In fact, they are unbeaten in their last seven at home against the Timbers.

Portland's last win against Dallas came back in June 2023 (1-0 at home), and while they have not won at Toyota Stadium since November 2018 (2-1), that victory was in the postseason.

#1898. Moreira discusses first Belgium goal, ‘special’ Milan group and learning in Italy: “I’ll always remember”

Last night, Diego Moreira scored his first goal for Belgium and AC Milan will be very happy to see their investment continuing to shine.

It’s fair to say that Moreira has been a revelation for Milan. His arrival came out of nowhere, with a deal first reported by FootballKush and then it was picked up by the biggest sources in football. His first appearance was a struggle against Juventus, but the rest, as they say, is history.

Goals have come regularly, with huge appearances that have defined the Rossoneri’s season already. For example, the goal against Inter, with two assists to accompany it. He’s perhaps been the signing of the season in Italy and there’d maybe be a conversation about Europe, too.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team…

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”

Then, in the mixed zone, he was also intercepted by MilanNews, where he also answered a few questions about the Rossoneri.

Diego, you scored in your first Milan derby, just like Kaká, Shevchenko, and Ronaldinho before you. How have you settled in at AC Milan?

“I’m very happy. At AC Milan, I’m surrounded by a special group, with many great players. Having them around me helps me a lot, especially in terms of experience. It’s true, the match against Inter was special. I’ll continue to work hard and give my best.”

Good in Serie A, bad in the Europa League: why this two-faced Milan?

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals…

“It’s something special, and we’re very happy. It was an important match, so winning and scoring was really nice.”
