#1897. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”

Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

We were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

Overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a big credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

We know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

It was my best [performance for Newcastle] so far. New manager, new role. I’m so pleased to be here. I hope today I showed I’m really happy.

It’s rough, especially 30 seconds before the end of the game, but that’s a huge step for us. That’s the mentality we need to have through the season. The manager came three weeks ago and gave us a lot of information. Now we show on the pitch we are ready for the season. We needed this win to make a statement but in the end we draw. We have so much to work on.

To be honest, I didn’t even hear the referee’s whistle. I had to look at him if I can go. I was practising a lot during the pre-season. We didn’t have any penalties during games, but in training. We need to take the positivity of the first game and move on.

More than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - new but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

If I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.

🗣️ "It's knee on knee, it's a foul"Micah Richards and Daniel Sturridge analyse Lewis Hall's foul which led to Liverpool's late penalty. pic.twitter.com/NRw406sTcZ

14 - Liverpool remain unbeaten on MD1 in the Premier League in each of the last 14 seasons (since 2013-14), the longest active run in the competition.Spirited. pic.twitter.com/3rluUnSBhu

I think they did the right thing, easy to say now of course, by not giving Isak the penalty. There is enough pressure on in the 96th minute without all that would have entailed. Nor was Isak having the best of games.

A familiar feeling after last season. Newcastle concede a last kick of the game penalty. Should have held on for the win. It was a soft penalty, Hall dangled out a knee rather than a leg and Munoz made sure he ran into it. But as soon as it's given on the field never going to be…

The points are shared, and Lewis Hall has his hands on his knees. Jaissle protests with the officials. This was a stirring home performance from Newcastle which should build confidence for the season ahead. An irrepressible showing from Wissa was the biggest positive. Iraola will be pleased to get back on the coach with a draw after what was quite a ragged Liverpool performance, their midfield balance looked off.

What a magnificent penalty from Szoboszlai, Hornicek had no chance, and Liverpool have surely snatched a point.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

What theatre that would be... Gakpo has the ball in his hands. But no, it’s going to be Szoboszlai.

With the last kick of the game, practically. Kerkez launched the ball forward, Van Dijk competed for a header, Munoz pounced on the seconds, and his pace carried enough threat to prompt Hall to step across the winger and make contact with his knee.

#NEWLIV – 90+6' The referee's call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR. REF: "He doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact". VAR: "It's knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty".

So, so poor from Frimpong who hesitates to put a cross in, takes a couple of unconvincing touches, and then commits a foul. Mac Allister. Wissa receives a standing ovation, replaced by Schar.

Gakpo runs down a blind alley, and it is another blunt Liverpool attack. Time running out for them now.

Liverpool corner, won by Lewis Koumas who lacked support but his cross deflects behind.

Hornicek palms away Szoboszlai’s delivery. This has been strong Premier League debut from the goalkeeper.

Newcastle have a throw deep in Liverpool territory after more good work from Wissa, and chaotic defending from Liverpool. Atwell has booked Gakpo for an earlier foul on Wissa.

There will be FIVE minutes of added time.

Murphy with another wonderful cross through the Liverpool six-yard box, but no player in black and white was gambling for a tap in. Liverpool just about still in with a sniff.

Cheers at St James’ Park as Thiaw ushers the ball behind as Kerkez tried to get in behind. Then Frimpong’s touch lets him down, not for the first time.

An aimless cross from Liverpool, and Munoz is penalised at the back post for a push. Liverpool have lacked clarity and intelligence in the last third today, but there is still time.

Big save by Alisson! He narrows the angle to deny Wissa the goal his performance deserves. How important could that prove to be? Liverpool have the ball again.

Liverpool with a long spell of possession in the final third, trying to tire Newcastle legs, but Frimpong’s cross is a little too high for Isak to generate any power with the header. Newcastle are just starting to sit in a touch.

Munoz runs down a blind alley, more sound defending from Lewis Hall and the Newcastle players can see the finish line now. They will be only too aware of how they lost this game in the last minute 12 months ago, though.

Szoboszlai shoots against the well, and the Araujo is booked for bundling over a Newcastle defender. Wissa thought he was away for Newcastle but the flag goes up for offside.

Frimpong does well to keep things alive for Liverpool, and there are half-hearted appeals for a handball penalty but Thiaw was down by his side. Another Liverpool sub: Lewis Koumas is on for Gravenberch.

The long throw is headed away, but Murphy catches Mac Allister and Liverpool have a free-kick in a crossing position. Though you never can tell with Szoboszlai around.

Here come those changes from Newcastle: Murphy and Bamba on for Elanga and Miley. Hall’s delivery from the free-kick won by Wissa was poor.

Liverpool have Newcastle penned in, but Munoz’s pass is overhit and Newcastle have a goal kick. Jaissle is about to introduce Jacob Murphy from the bench. Wissa, Newcastle’s best player by a stretch, does well to win a free-kick high up the pitch from Szoboszlai.

Araujo is on for Jacquet at the back for Liverpool, who have just threatened again. Szoboszlai hacked down but the referee waved play on, and Kerkez could not get enough curl on his cross or else Isak would have had a free header.

Willock lifts in a teasing cross from the right, Alisson palms the ball back into danger, and Ramsey cracks a shot wide of the post. Hard to say whether this game is going 3-1 or 2-2 but the scoring is surely not over.

Was that Isak’s moment? Gakpo rolls the ball back to Isak in a good shooting position just inside the box, but he slices his left-footed effort well over the bar. More cheers from the Newcastle fans.

Newcastle really should have three! Defence-splitting pass from Miley to release Hall, who feeds a teasing cross into the six-yard box, but Wissa could only get studs on it. Better connection and that was a goal. Liverpool so fragile at the back, though.

Stuart Atwell has been guessing on decisions throughout this game, and Jacob Ramsey has just been booked for what looked a clean challenge on Isak, who produced a lovely turn initially. Newcastle survive the free-kick.

But then Gakpo has acres of space to run into, but Botman saves the day in the box. The game is haywire at the moment.

Here come the Liverpool changes: Ngumoha, who was the match-winner last season here, Wirtz are the players off, replaced by Munoz and Mac Allister.

Liverpool will be kicking themselves, they had Newcastle on the ropes. Iraola is preparing a triple sub. Willock was the goalscorer, but it was also a brilliant assist from Wissa.

The equaliser had been coming but that was really poor from a defensive perspective as everyone backed off Cody Gakpo and let him pick his spot.

You also have to question the decision to keep Will Osula on. He was obviously struggling to move freely and it has meant Newcastle did not have an out ball.

But, just as I was going to be critical of manager Matthias Jassile one of his substitutes puts Newcastle back in front and it a brilliant goal. Magnificent build up play from Wissa, who skipped away from three Liverpool players, but it is even better from Joe Willock who takes the pass in his stride, shows great skill t o take it on jis stride and away from Frimpong and the finish is sublime, curled into the bottom corner.

Jaissle can claim that as a magical substitution, but it is superb individual goal from Joe Willock. Another Newcastle counter-attack, Wissa does brilliantly to wriggle away from three players in midfield, and Willock dribbles inside Frimpong before arcing a shot into the far corner. Outstanding finish.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

Jaissle with a double sub immediately after conceding: Joe Willock and Jacob Ramsey are on, replacing William Osula and Sean Steur who was a little slack on the Gakpo goal.

The game is one-way traffic, Liverpool looking to turn the screw.

The man linked with a move to Spurs all summer has equalised for Liverpool. He had a sighter a few minutes earlier, and it was too easy for Gakpo to receive the ball behind Newcastle’s midfield, and he had time to pick out the far corner with a clean hit from outside the box. Game on.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

Just two touches inside the Newcastle penalty area from Isak so far, he has been subdued. Nice idea from Gakpo, chopping inside from the left, and curling a shot not far wide of the top corner.

Good defending from Lewis Hall up against Ngumoha, before Van Dijk passes the ball straight of play. Wissa wanted a free-kick for a challenge from behind by Gravenberch but the referee judged he touched the ball first.

Scramble at the back post from the Liverpool corner, but then a loose touch from Wirtz prompts a Newcastle break and there was a chance for Elanga to dribble into the box but he put the breaks on.

The game is already really stretched, holes appearing in Liverpool’s midfield. Wissa’s poked through ball towards Osula was just a tad overhit.

Liverpool have made a sharp start from kick off, winning a corner.

Just because it is a manager’s first game, we shouldn’t pull our punches. That was a scandalous first half performance from Liverpool and there is absolutely no difference in watching them now compared to what they offered through much of last season. Maybe the disappointment wasn’t about the man in the dugout. Maybe it was about the players wearing the Red shirt.

5 & 18 - 5 - Liverpool have conceded in the opening five minutes on MD1 of a Premier League season for the very first time.The Reds are winless in 18 Premier League away games when falling 1-0 behind (D6 L12) since beating Crystal Palace 2-1 in December 2023.Baptism. pic.twitter.com/K1HF2wNRVP

Newcastle will be delighted to go in leading the game at half time but there were some worrying signs before the break.

They had stopped getting up the pitch and were invited a lot of pressure from Liverpool. Will Osula has clearly picked up an injury – he took a whack on his achilles midway through the half – and will surely need to be replaced by Nick Woltemade in the second half with Yoane Wissa moving up top.

Alexander Isak has been on the receiving end of a number of heavy tackles and has looked pretty miserable so far on his return to St James’ Park.

But Liverpool are not going to keep getting into dangerous positions and fail to capitalise on them. Things for Matthias Jaissle to sort out before the second half.

LFC Midfield all bombing forward happened all pre season, madness!

Plenty of possession for Liverpool, but not enough cutting edge of crispness in their play in the final third. On top of that problem, they were vulnerable to Newcastle’s pace and direct play early on although that threat abated as the half progressed. Jaissle will be delighted with the commitment and application of his players, but Osula may have to come off with a knock.

Isak hooks a pass towards Frimpong straight out of play, causing much mirth among the home fans.

Foul given against Wissa on Gravenberch, and the Newcastle forward needs to be careful on a yellow. I’m not sure there was any contact at all. Wissa drags a shot across the face of Liverpool’s goal and wide.

Gravenberch with a speculative shot which is blocked, before Dedic blasts the ball off Gakpo to win a goal kick. Dan Burn is watching on from the stands, Newcastle’s new club captain who is absent because of a rolled ankle. Also up there in the gods is England manager Thomas Tuchel.

Much better cross from Frimpong, but Dedic clears at the back post for a Liverpool corner. Danger as Gakpo flicks the ball on at the neat post, and the ball bounces off Botman and behind for another corner. Gravenberch tries a cute reverse pass towards Isak, but it deflects through to Hornicek. Isak has been ever so quiet.

William Osula is hobbling up top for Newcastle, which is a worry because has been a menace so far. The same can be said of Yoane Wissa who is having a stormer as a second striker, dropping into midfield at times.

Stuart Atwell being a little card happy, now Lewis Miley is shown a yellow for a foul on Gravenberch. Just looked a regulation midfield foul, not sure a booking was necessary.

Osula took the free-kick, straight into the wall, but his follow up effort deflects off Szoboszlai and behind for a corner. Excellent delivery from Lewis Hall, cleared by Van Dijk.

Wirtz and Isak do well down the left to start a Liverpool counter with runners forward, but Frimpong’s delivery from the right is atrocious.

Liverpool starting to monopolise possession, without a crafty final pass. Kerkez has been booked for holding Elanga, who is giving him a going over on Newcastle’s right flank.

Then Barnes rolls inside Frimpong and drives inside, and the Liverpool right-back is booked for a challenge from behind. May well have been a harsh call, both plays were grasping for a piece of shirt.

Both of Liverpool’s full-backs on yellows now.

Wissa booked for a mistimed challenge, and Liverpool have a free-kick 30 yards out. Szoboszlai is thinking about a shot... but he blasts his shot straight into the wall.

Osula then does very well to make it stick and drag Newcastle up the pitch but the move fizzles out.

It’s an experience in itself watching Andoni Iraola on the sideline. He’s going to have clocked up 10,000 steps for sure by the final whistle and his increasing animation is indicative of Liverpool’s anaemic start. You would expect Liverpool to score at some point but this is a team that has lots of questions to answer.

Isak down on the turf after a strong challenge by Lewis Hall, no foul given much to the delight of the Newcastle fans.

Then the home team cut through Liverpool again, Wissa with a glorious outside of the foot pass behind Jacquet for the run of Osula, but the Liverpool defender just about got a toe to the ball as the striker closed in on Alisson. Great challenge in the end from the wrong side.

Nice counter-movement between Elanga and Dedic the right-back. Elanga faked to drop inside, taking Kerkez and Gakpo with him, and Miley’s switch found Dedic on the outside. Cross is blocked, and Newcastle have a corner. Cleared, and then a poor Szoboszlai pass is blocked when there was a chance to release Wirtz on the counter.

It feels like all the 50:50s are dropping Newcastle’s way at the moment. It has been a very energetic start, the question is whether that is sustainable across the game so early in the season. The tempo will surely drop at some point.

Peter Beardsley, Tino Asprilla and Shaka Hislop among Keegan’s former players watching on.

Hornicek with his first big save of the game, tipping Wirtz’s shot around the post. Newcastle failed to deal with a Kerkez cross and the ball dropped to the German for a snap shot. Newcastle defend the corner.

“There’s only one greedy b-----d,” is the chant from the Newcastle fans (aimed at Isak, for the uninitiated).

Wissa goes down looking for a foul but nothing doing, but there are cheers from the home fans as Isak is beaten to a header and then Sean Steur turns away from pressure well in midfield. There is more bite about the home team in the challenges than Liverpool, Jaissle will be delighted with this.

Echoes of last season with Liverpool’s defence looking suspect against direct play, Alisson with an unconvincing intervention outside his penalty area after the ball held up. He is fortunate that Wissa did not connect with the volley when there was a chance to lob the goalkeeper.

What a difference a year makes. Anthony Elanga was played in on goal against Aston Villa on his Premier League debut for Newcastle United 12 months ago. He looked nervous and hit a tame effort too close to the goalkeeper.

It is fair to say that was a sign of things to come for the winger who endured a miserable first season on Tyneside following a high-profile £55m move from Nottingham Forest. He looked drained of confidence and lacked the composure and technical ability to succeed in black and white stripes.

Fast forward 12 months and he has just taken a very similar chance against Liverpool. The speed of Will Osula sent the visiting defence into retreat, and his pace and excellent first touch set up the chance, which he finished clinically.

That was the player Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer. It was the player Newcastle supporters thought was going to offer a major upgrade in the right wing position.

If Elanga has a better season this time around it will be a huge boost to new manager Matthias Jaissle.

Elanga vs Kerkez is a match-up which looks advantageous for Newcastle, the Liverpool left-back is at full tilt to get back and by a foul after a lofted Wissa pass over his head towards the rapid Sweden winger.

This is a very open game already, and Liverpool are back on the front foot. Szoboszlai whips in a free-kick which appears to glance of Van Dijk’s head, but the referee awards a corner. Hall clears, but Newcastle do not clear their lines and Gakpo’s shot is blocked by Thiaw.

Liverpool caught out on the break, but it is a really well-executed goal from Newcastle’s perspective. Gravenberch should have let fly at the other end, but after the move broke down Osula was able to receive in space and turn to face Van Dijk and Jacquet. He waited for the support of Elanga to arrive, and he burned down the outside of Kerkez. Well-weighted pass put him through, and the finish across Alisson was ideal.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

Lewis Hall wins a challenge at the edge of the box which receives a roar of approval from the crowd, but Liverpool quickly settle into a long spell of possession, with Gravenberch turning away from pressure, but neglecting to shoot.

This already has the feel of a very helter-skelter game. Newcastle won a free-kick inside 20 seconds, clipped into the penalty area but it was claimed by Alisson. Then a Liverpool attack swept from one end to the other with Wirtz’s shot blocked at the edge of the box. This should be tasty.

That roar turns to vociferous boos as Alexander Isak takes the kick-off.

They would have still been clapping until tomorrow if the whistle hadn’t been blown by referee Stuart Attwell to start the game but the flip from adulation for Kevin Keegan to absolute vitriol towards Alexander Isak was incredible. 50,000 in black and white are singing a song aimed at him. The only two words we can get away with printing are “ole, ole!” - use your imagination for what might have preceded it!

A period of applause for Kevin Keegan at St James' Park 👏❤️ pic.twitter.com/AsSGOkpVPN

There is a minute’s applause for Keegan, which ends with a defending roar.

Liverpool have just taken to the field for their warm up, predictably to a back drop of pantomime booing. But there is a nice touch from the club, as each member of Andoni Iraola’s squad is wearing a jersey with “Keegan 7” on the back. It’s going to be a day of heavy emotion.

Alan Shearer was one of those fans holding up a white card:

The Keegan quote on the Newcastle banner is: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should, we should all be dreamers at heart. Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that’, but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well, I say, ‘Why not?’”

Banners are being unfurled in the Gallowgate End. Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce are in the stands, and Les Ferdinand is pitchside speaking on Sky.

As you know it’s a transition phase and a huge challenge. There will be some activity in the transfer market new week, hopefully, but we go for it, we are as ready as we can be. That’s something we want to show the fans, we want to go all in.

As soon as I saw him on the pitch, I was falling in love. He is a great guy with great potential.

I’m not worried. As a manager, a player or a squad, if it is against you you want to play this kind of games.

Difficult call, Jeremy has very good skills with the ball, without the ball they will be very demanding today, playing against Wissa and Osula.

Alexander Isak is going to be in for the sort of hostile afternoon unseen in English football for years.

Not since Michael Owen has a player left Newcastle and been so universally despised. Owen was accused of ducking out of a relegation battle to ensure he secured a lucrative free transfer move after an injury-ravaged spell in the North East.

If anything, Isak was even worse, He went on strike, refusing to play for the club again, despite having three years left on his contract, in order to force a move to Liverpool. It felt like the ultimate betrayal and crossed a line with Geordies. They will love you and worship players as good as Isak, but if you behave like the Sweden international did you become the ultimate villain.

Isak was a superb player in black and white stripes, arguably their best since the takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund in 2021. He was top goalscorer two years running and was the focal point of Eddie Hower’s attack as they qualified for the Champions League twice and won the Carabao Cup.

He could have been a Geordie legend, but he left in such an ugly and acrimonious fashion. Isak forced Newcastle to buckle from their not for sale stance, rejecting a pay rise and a new contract, insisting he would never play for the club again even if they refused to sell him, that he will be tarnished forever.

It is sad in many ways and shows the ugly side of the game. I’m told he does regret the manner of his exit, especially his falling out with Howe. They have not spoken since. It has weighed heavily on him since his move to Anfield.

Looks like Rio Ngumoha will play on the right flank with Cody Gakpo left, Wirtz in the No 10 role behind Isak.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Frimpong, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Gravenberch, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak

The Reds to take on Newcastle in our season opener ✊ #NEWLIV

Barnes, Wissa, Osula and Elanga start in what could be a front four. Lewis Miley and Sean Steur, just 20 and 18 respectively, will need to get through an immense amount of work in midfield.

Newcastle United XI: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Miley, Steur; Elanga, Wissa, Barnes; Osula

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Bobby Moncur are the representatives of both clubs with wreaths, and Shola Ameobi is behind Dalglish. Ian Rush is also in attendance, who spent one season on Tyneside in the twilight of his career when Dalglish was the manager.

There will be a powerful expression of unity between Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters in memory of their shared icon, Kevin Keegan, before this afternoon’s game.

A man who meant so much to both clubs: a phenomenal player for Liverpool and a force of nature who transformed Newcastle as both a player and a manager.

The cooperation between the two to ensure St James’ Park can deliver a special tribute to a remarkable figure in English football has been heartwarming.

The sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan means that for the first time since Liverpool came into existence in 1892, the prospect of them going through the season without fielding a player who was born in the city for a game is real. That will surely sting Liverpool fans more than most, given the city’s strong sense of regional identity. You can read more on the subject in this article by Dominic King. Trent on loan in January, anyone?

He has also not sugar-coated anything. Jaissle knows he is up against it. Time is the enemy, given how late he arrived in pre-season and he understands the size of the task ahead.

These are early days, but the energy and purpose he has brought to the job have impressed everyone at all levels of the club. Clear communication is at the heart of everything. He explains what he expects, what he needs and what has to be done, no matter who the conversation is with.

It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.Full team news on the way shortly.

#1896. Tottenham women confirm executive shake-up as new sporting director appointed

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham have confirmed the appointment of a new director of women’s football, which comes as part of a thorough shake-up of the team’s management.

Kim Pedersen will take over the running of Spurs women from December 7, joining from Danish side Brondby.

He will bring to north London nearly 15 years of experience in football coaching and administration, across both the men’s and women’s game. In his most recent role, the Norwegian helped Brondby become Denmark’s first fully professional women’s outfit.

He joins a Tottenham side on something of an upward trajectory. The club has been steadily improving since the appointment of Martin Ho last year and has a clear aspiration to qualify for the Champions League, though they look set to fall short of that target this term despite heavy investment in the summer transfer window.

Pedersen’s appointment comes some six months on from the departure of the long-serving Andy Rogers, formerly managing director of the women’s team, whose 24-year spell with the club ended in May.

Speaking in an interview with the club after signing, Pedersen set his sights on helping Tottenham to upset the WSL’s heavyweights.

Also joining Tottenham women alongside Pedersen are Lucy Button, newly appointed the women’s growth director, and Hannah Sheridan, the women’s director of performance and operations.

Tottenham’s director of football operations Rafi Moersen said: “We have made a deliberate decision to evolve the way we lead Women's football at Tottenham Hotspur, establishing dedicated leadership across three critical areas: football, performance and operations, and commercial growth.

“This is about building the foundations for sustained success, on and off the pitch, with clear accountability, specialist leadership and the ambition to accelerate our progress.

“Together, these appointments, alongside continued investment in our infrastructure, represent an important step in our commitment to building a successful and sustainable future for Women's football at Tottenham Hotspur.”

#1895. Mauricio Pochettino 'honoured' and 'privileged' to be at Man United as Red Devils reign officially begins

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:26, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 15:27

Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United's new head coach, with the Argentine arriving at the club's Carrington training complex.

The Argentine oversaw USA's 2-0 win over Haiti in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final, which kicked off at midnight on Tuesday UK time, before flying to Manchester to begin work with the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino's time as head coach of Man United has now officially started, with the club posting a video of the 54-year-old arriving on their X account.

"Very excited to be here. It's an honour. It's a privilege to be in this amazing club. Looking forward to starting work," said Pochettino.

He's here. Welcome to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino! ??? https://t.co/MOhRCv79hq

Man United appointed Pochettino as their new head coach at the end of last week, but the club agreed that he could finish his November commitments with the USA before arriving on Wednesday, as the Red Devils prepare for Sunday's Premier League game at Liverpool.

The 54-year-old's assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino travelled to Manchester earlier this week.

Pochettino is set to speak to the media at Carrington on Friday afternoon.

Players who have represented their countries during the international break will arrive at Carrington from Thursday, so it is a quick turnaround ahead of the Liverpool clash.

Pochettino will hardly have time to take stock after the Liverpool game, as Man United will then head to Portugal at the start of next week to prepare to take on Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League.

The Argentine led the USA to the last-16 stage of the 2026 World Cup and also reached the 2025 Gold Cup final during his time in charge.

In an exit statement on Instagram, Pochettino said: "I am proud of what we achieved. When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team.

"This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally.

"Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

"I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves."

Pochettino has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, while he has left his USA role with a record of 23 wins, two draws and 12 defeats from his 37 matches at the helm.

#1894. Revealed: Matthias Jaissle’s eleventh-hour bid to stop Bruno Guimaraes’ Arsenal switch

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Matthias Jaissle made a last-ditch attempt to convince Bruno Guimaraes to snub offers from Arsenal and stay at Newcastle.

Guimaraes signed for Arsenal in a £75m deal in August - just three days after Jaissle’s appointment as Eddie Howe’s replacement - calling time on a four-year association with Newcastle, where he was a favourite of the club’s passionate fanbase.

The Magpies were desperate to keep Guimaraes on Tyneside and dug their heels in to prevent the deal, but eventually gave in once it became clear the player had set his heart on the transfer. He has since scored twice in 14 appearances for the Gunners.

And, speaking ahead of Guimaraes’ first return to St James’ Park, Jaissle explained Guimaraes had already decided to leave before he was appointed Eddie Howe’s replacement.

But that did not stop him from trying to convince the Brazilian to stick around.

“I met Bruno for a short time only,” the German explained. “But the decision was already made. I tried my best to persuade him but his decision was made.”

Jaissle continued: “We counted on him as a leader last season, I just tried to explain the role he would have had with us.

“The decision was already made, he informed me. I’d had the information beforehand, and I had been informed. It is my job to do my best anyway and at least I can look in the mirror and say I tried.”

It remains to be seen what kind of reception Guimaraes will receive on return to Tyneside, but Harvey Barnes has already made clear that his former team-mates are keen to get one over on him.

Jaissle, though, called on his squad to keep their heads: “If you face the champions, that is motivation enough. We are playing at home in front of our fans; they can be the twelfth man. The fans can give us so much power and support. This is a great opportunity, a big challenge.”

#1893. Man United transfer news: Red Devils urged to sell Bruno Fernandes and bring in 37-goal attacker as his replacement

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 15:57, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 16:00

Former Manchester United captain Ashley Young has urged the Red Devils to sell captain Bruno Fernandes next year and bring in Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White as his replacement.

Fernandes' future with the Red Devils is currently the subject of much speculation, with the Portugal international's contract at Old Trafford due to expire next summer.

Man United do have the option to activate a further year to take the 32-year-old to the summer of 2028, but it is understood that Fernandes has rejected the chance to sign a fresh deal with the club.

The Portuguese had an outstanding 2025-26 Premier League season, scoring nine goals and registering 21 assists in 35 appearances, while he has six goals and three assists in 14 appearances for the Red Devils this term.

Fernandes has struggled to show his best form for much of the campaign, though, and a departure next year is seen as possible.

Young, who played for Man United between 2011 and 2020, has urged the 20-time English champions to make a move for Forest's Gibbs-White.

The 26-year-old has scored 37 goals and registered 38 assists in 180 matches for Forest in all competitions, including one goal and three assists in nine Premier League outings this term.

“Bruno has been fantastic for Manchester United. He has been, and no one can say that he hasn’t,” Young told Standard Sport.

“There's obviously been a few things that have come up of late. If a club like Manchester United are going to build a team around him, he's going to be 33 next year.

“If it was me, I would be looking at going to get another number 10 and build it around him. I'd go and get Morgan Gibbs-White. I think he's got 18 months left on his contract.

"He's established in the Premier League, he’s a leader, he's showing his qualities at Nottingham Forest. And I'm sure Nottingham Forest won't thank me for saying that.”

Gibbs-White has long been linked with a move away from Forest, but he signed a new deal with the club in the summer of 2025 after a proposed switch to Tottenham Hotspur failed to materialise.

The Englishman is surely in line for a move to an elite club in the not too distant future, and he would be an ideal signing for Man United given his skill set and Premier League experience.

Man United will be active in the summer of 2027, and if Fernandes moves on, then Gibbs-White could be the perfect replacement for the Portuguese.

#1892. Pochettino determined to ‘change things’ at Man Utd

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino believes it is a "mistake" to solely focus on Manchester United's current predicament, and vows to "change things" at the club.

Pochettino began his tenure as United boss on Wednesday, leaving his position as United States head coach after signing off with a win in the Concacaf Nations League quarter-finals against Haiti.

He is tasked with improving United's current position, with the team sitting 18th in the Premier League table after the first 10 games.

The Red Devils have won just one of their first 10 matches in the league (D5 L4), while they are winless in eight Premier League matches for just the second time, also doing so in April/May 2025.

By the time United kick off against Liverpool in Pochettino's first game in charge, they will have been in the drop zone for 15 consecutive days – their longest run of days in the top-flight drop zone since September/October 1986 (28 days).

But Pochettino does not want to focus on the negatives, instead choosing to be optimistic about what United could do.

"It's a mistake to see the situation," Pochettino told United's social channels. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"It's about to start to act and to change things, and to try to affect, in a good way, all the areas, to try to really believe that we can recover that feeling about to win.

"The most important thing is for us to start to work hard to recover that feeling. That feeling is about being winners, to win games, to perform. But that is not only to talk about winning."

The importance of Sunday's fixture isn't lost on Mauricio

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 19, 2026

Reports suggest Pochettino will have a say in whatever business United do in the January transfer window, but he has over a month until he can add reinforcements to his squad.

United have 10 games to play before the end of the calendar year, and the Argentinian is determined to get the best out of his current crop of players.

"The best request that we can have, the players that we have, and we need to love the players that we have," Pochettino added.

"We need to support the players; we need to provide all the tools for their performance.

"It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the possibility to translate all their talent on the field."

Pochettino will be the first-ever United manager to see his first league game come against rivals, Liverpool.

Just one of the Red Devils' last nine managers (incl. caretakers) has lost his first Premier League game of a spell in charge of the club (W4 D4), with Erik ten Hag losing 1-2 to Brighton in August 2022.

Though Liverpool are the favourites to win – with the Opta supercomputer giving them a 57.3% chance of victory on Sunday – Pochettino has his eyes on three points.

"We are going to go there, to Anfield, with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United," he said.

"We need to make sure that we are brave, and we are protagonists, and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool."

Jurgen Kloppai??i??s countrymen are well versed with the appeal of quick fixes. They once allowed one of historyai??i??s most hated figures to rise to power. Of course, when Adolf Hitler was rapidly gaining popularity in Germany, he didnai??i??t do it by telling his people he would bring about the Second World War so soon after the first one had concluded. No, he did it by promising quick fixes. In a country reeling from the effects of the first World War and later the onset of the Great Depression, the promises of a party that would swoop in and fix issues ranging from more practical ones like unemployment, to rather more emotional ones like the loss of national pride after the defeat in the previous World War, was welcome to the masses.

Liverpool FC is a little like post World War I Germany — a lot of pride, but very little recent success to validate all that ego. As a result, the fans are in a constant state of impatience, always hoping the next player or the next manager will be the one to lead them back to the glory days. Thereai??i??s nothing wrong with having hope, but it needs to be balanced with practicality. Overly inflated expectations almost always tend to blow up in oneai??i??s face.

Jurgen Klopp is quite different from the former Nazi party leader of course. From day 1, heai??i??s been trying to temper expectations rather than fuel them.

a Expectations can be a really big problem. Itai??i??s like a backpack ai??i?? 20 kilos more! Iai??i??m not here to promise that against Tottenham you will see the new LFC, but maybe some of it. Everything in life takes time, the only thing nobody gives time is development.a ai??i?? Jurgen Klopp

Instead itai??i??s the fans that are overburdening the manager and the team with their dreams of an overnight turnover of fortunes. Insanity is doing the same things over and over again and expecting different results. This greatly reflects his vision and ability to curb any impulse to seek a ready-made answer in the transfer market.

If you include the loan and youth players, Liverpoolai??i??s squad strength is pretty massive. So there is little sense in buying loads of new players, unless thereai??i??s conclusive evidence that the current crop canai??i??t cut it at the highest level. Seeing how itai??i??s still early days in the reign of Klopp, itai??i??s unlikely he would have been able to reach that conclusion about too many of his players.

That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. #1890. Mazzara: ‘A core of 16-18 high level players’ – Cardinale hopes to take Milan to new levels

Gerry Cardinale has invested heavily in AC Milan recently and there are no plans to slow down anytime soon.

Since the restructuring of the vendor loan, Cardinale has completely changed his ownership style. More actively involved, the American has seemingly fallen in love with the club and has become desperate to see it succeed.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Glimpses were seen before the mercato, with him regularly visiting the training ground. However, his work since then – spending €150 million on transfers and attending every Serie A game so far – shows the level of dedication he has to the cause.

In January, the American is expected to spend heavily, too. A €70 million bid for Endrick is being prepared, whilst he is also determined to sign Goncalo Inacio. It’s clear that he wants to raise the level of the starters and those who will contribute from the bench.

In an editorial for MilanNews today, Pietro Mazzara looked at the current squad and what Cardinale plans to do.

“AC Milan’s transfer market is poised for significant events because Gerry Cardinale has no intention of stopping. His comments in recent days, both public and private, are a clear statement of what the AC Milan owner intends to do to bring AC Milan back to the top.

“Whether he succeeds or not will only be determined by time and the type of decisions he makes, but he certainly has the desire, vision, and financial resources. One can expect anything from someone who beat out Netflix for the Warner Bros. acquisition.

“Among the many things he has learned is that the climate of mediocrity surrounding results has undermined the mentality of a club and an environment that, instead, must strive to always be at the top.

“But returning to those levels requires several factors: a clear decision-making structure (which will be finalised by Markus Krösche, who will always report to Cardinale, who will always have the final say and be involved in negotiations), strong players in the squad, a political presence in the halls of power, a connection with the fans, and credibility.

“What may seem like slogans in themselves are actually manifestos that one can legitimately believe or not. The only way to evaluate Cardinale’s work is to observe how he operates and then draw conclusions.

“He’s fired up, and between January and next summer there will be some serious transfer campaigns. The reason is simple: there’s a need to significantly raise the squad’s level, creating a core of 16-18 players of a certain caliber who can be joined by young players to develop and develop.

“This is why Milan will be looking for not only technically strong players, but also leaders who can complement those already in the Milan core group.

“It’s crucial to raise the team’s personality, including strong personalities who can provide a different kind of motivation during the day-to-day at Milanello. These players, inevitably, cost money, but Cardinale doesn’t want to set limits.

“This doesn’t mean Milan will sign a player worth one hundred million euros, but it does mean they can continue along the operational path laid out by Diego Moreira. All of this is in concert and in line with Ruben Amorim, who is fiercely defended by the AC Milan owner and with whom he intends to begin a long-term relationship.

“And the vision is to acquire the Van Dijks in the pre-prime phase rather than signing them at 35 (assuming, for the sake of argument, that I’d sign someone like that now).

“In my opinion, a Sandro Tonali- style signing is needed. And it’s not out of the question that Milan could try to bring him back in the coming years, even though he currently plays for a club as complex to negotiate with as Tottenham.

“Meanwhile, discussions are ongoing to finalise the renewal of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse.”

#1889. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1888. Man United news: KMI Panel delivers surprise verdict over Aston Villa equaliser

By Darren Plant | 18 Nov 2026 16:00

The KMI Panel has unanimously claimed that Manchester United's decisive equaliser against Aston Villa was correctly awarded.

In the final Premier League match before the November international break, the Red Devils and Villans played out a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford.

Villa twice held two-goal advantages - at 2-0 and 4-2 - before United scored twice in added-on time to earn a deserved share of the spoils.

However, there were question marks over whether Patrick Dorgu's last-gasp equaliser should have stood.

United goalkeeper Senne Lammens, who had joined the attack for a corner, seemingly deliberately made contact with opposite number Zion Suzuki without making an attempt for the ball.

Despite it appearing clear that Lammens's only intention was to make contact with Suzuki, it has been deemed that the referee and VAR were correct not to award or advise a foul.

A five-person KMI Panel all determined that a foul had not been committed by Lammens, subsequently leading to VAR not being required to intervene.

The KMI Panel said: "Although Lammens turned away from the ball, the contact he made on Suzuki was not impactful."

Aston Villa chief Damian Vidagany took to social media in the day after the match to claim that all 20 Premier League clubs had been informed before the start of the season that such an action from any player would be penalised.

The incident was one which brought up a genuine debate over whether the goal should have stood, but the fact that the KMI Panel voted unanimously against a foul being committed could open a can of worms.

Managers and players will, logically, now attempt to replicate the level of interference from Lammens, aware that they could avoid punishment from officials.

#1887. ​Women’s Super League predictions: Arsenal, Chelsea and Man City backed as big favourites on MD11

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The 2026-27 Women's Super League season is already 10 games in, and both ends of the table are taking shape.

Charlton Athletic remain without a point to their name at the foot of the standings, but above them, Birmingham City, Crystal Palace, Brighton and Liverpool are all clustered within five points of each other.

At the summit, Chelsea sit one point above reigning champions Manchester City, while London City Lionesses are flying high in third place.

Arsenal have a lot of ground to make up, but they are made the biggest favourites for MD11 when they host West Ham this weekend.

Chelsea face Liverpool, and Man City take on Tottenham in some intriguing matchups. Here, we use Opta insights and the supercomputer to look ahead to the WSL action.

It's heating up at the top of the #BarclaysWSL table https://t.co/weclTxN0Gy

— Barclays Women's Super League (@BarclaysWSL) November 16, 2026

Chelsea have won 17 games against Liverpool in the WSL (D4 L5), their joint-most victories over any one side in the competition (also 17 wins v Everton).

And Opta's model is forecasting another Chelsea victory at St Helens Stadium, with the Blues handed a whopping 70.4% chance of victory.

That makes them the most favoured away team on MD11 by some distance, with Liverpool's 13.1% win probability coming in higher than only two other sides.

Liverpool have won only five of their 26 WSL meetings with Chelsea (D4 L17), though each of the most recent four of those have come at home, most recently in May 2024 (4-3).

Chelsea have won each of their last six WSL away games, only once before having a longer winning run on the road in the competition, eight straight wins between August 2015 and September 2016.

The Blues' expected goal difference of +25.3 is more than twice that of any other side in the WSL this term, with London City next on +11.7. Sonia Bompastor's team have both attempted the most shots (228) and faced the fewest (72), taking more than three for every shot allowed.

It feels unfair to label London City as a surprise package this season, given the investment into their squad this past summer. Can a team with a Ballon d'Or holder in their ranks really be considered a surprise package?

Putellas has created 18 chances, provided one assist and scored three goals already in the WSL, and her form has been integral to London City sitting in third place ahead of hosting Crystal Palace.

London City are the clear favourites, with a win likelihood of 67.2% to Palace's 14.8%. There is an 18% chance of a draw.

Palace have, however, won their last two away league games against London City without conceding (1-0 in 2022-23, 2-0 in 2023-24), though they have already lost away to the Lionesses in this season's Players Cup (2-4).

But Palace are winless in their last 14 away games in the WSL (D5 L9), since a 2-0 victory at Leicester City in October 2024. Having drawn each of their first three away matches this season, the Eagles have lost both of their last two.

London City have won six of their last seven WSL home games (L1), scoring at least twice in every victory.

Manchester United are fourth, eight points behind leaders Chelsea, and they are the favourites to take three points against next-to-bottom Birmingham.

The Red Devils have a 60.1% win probability, while Birmingham have a 19.2% chance.

After a difficult start under new boss Eva Olid, United are unbeaten in their last eight WSL games (W5 D3), having lost their opening two this season.

The Red Devils have conceded just four goals during this run, compared with seven in those first two matches, and have kept a clean sheet in each of their last three.

Ella Toone has scored (three goals) or assisted (two assists) in all four of United's WSL games against Birmingham. No fixture has been played more often in the competition with the same player registering a goal involvement in every meeting.

Spurs are unbeaten in three league games, and that form has taken them to fifth in the standings.

However, they are not given much of a chance against Manchester City, who have a 74% win probability. Spurs come out on top in just 10.8% of the supercomputer's simulations.

City have won 12 of their 13 WSL games against Tottenham, with the exception being a 2-1 home defeat in September 2021.

And Spurs have lost six of their last seven away matches against City in all competitions (W1), averaging over four goals conceded per defeat (26 in six).

City have won each of their last 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026; only Chelsea have ever won more home matches in a calendar year, winning 11 in both 2022 and 2023.

And while the supercomputer expects it to be close between Charlton and Aston Villa, the Villans are anticipated to take the points (42.6% to Charlton's 32%). There is a 25.4% probability of a draw.

Charlton have conceded nine set-piece goals in the WSL this season, at least three more than any other side and accounting for 30% of their goals against (9/30). Six have come from corners, also the most in the division, while the Addicks are yet to score via one themselves.

Everton sit eighth on the back of three straight draws, but those all came against teams above them in the standings (Spurs, Chelsea and Man Utd).

They now host Brighton. Everton have never drawn four consecutive games in the competition, with their only other run of three coming in their first three WSL fixtures in April 2011.

The Toffees are the favourites, with a 43.5% win probability, but at 26.8% this is the game that is most likely to be a draw, with Brighton's chances ranked at 29.7%.

Everton have kept a clean sheet in three of their last five WSL home games, as often as across their 23 home matches prior; the Toffees themselves could go goalless in back-to-back home matches in the league for the first time since November 2023, however.

Between the 2018-19 and 2023-24 seasons, the head-to-head record between Everton and Brighton in the WSL was perfectly balanced with four wins each (D4) – since then, however, the Seagulls have won all four of their top-flight meetings with the Toffees.

West Ham have won three of their last five WSL games (L2), having won just one of their opening five this season (L4); the Hammers' four victories are already three more than they had recorded at the same stage last term (one).

Arsenal are the first team to draw each of their opening five home games of a WSL season, with the last four all finishing 1-1. The Gunners are nevertheless unbeaten in their last 24 home matches in the competition (W16 D8), since a defeat to Chelsea in October 2024.

But they will now be looking to bounce back from a disappointing 2-0 home loss to Lyon in the Women's Champions League on Thursday.

The Gunners have won all eight of their WSL home games against West Ham by an aggregate score of 27-8, always scoring at least twice in those matches.

#1885. Man United confirm five departures following Mauricio Pochettino arrival

By Matt Law | 18 Nov 2026 16:26, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 16:32

Manchester United have officially confirmed that staff members Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate have left the club alongside Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils made the decision to sack Carrick as head coach last week, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been confirmed as his replacement.

Pochettino officially started work as Man United manager on Wednesday, with the Argentine arriving at Carrington following the completion of his duties with the USA.

Man United have confirmed that Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino have arrived alongside Pochettino.

Meanwhile, five staff members have left alongside Carrick.

"Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian," read a statement from Man United.

"Pochettino’s appointment was announced last Friday with an agreement he’ll begin on 18 November, once he had fulfilled his duties with the US Men’s National Team.

"Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA.

"Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.

"The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

"We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future."

Man United will continue their Premier League campaign against Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, and Pochettino will be in the dug-out for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino has taken charge of a team currently down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up only eight points from their first 10 matches of the season.

#1883. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.
